name: NSKY Merna
notes: Mid-range centric better OG EJ07 with the best vocals I've heard so far - comes with "free" custom fit/shell if you want. Insane staging super wide, scales great, even more immersive than OG EJ07s. Makes you ascend and lose track of time.

name: SUBTONIC STORM 2022
notes: Second best IEM I've ever heard. Best timbre. Super natural. TOTL tech. It's just good. That's all.

name: LETSHUOER Cadenza 12
notes: Pre-Production Unit with a different tuning. A better version of the U12T vocal/tuning wise, no mid scoop and wonkiness. (#1 or #2 vocals for me). Vocals are sweet, extended, open, airy, but also never fatiguing, and naturally weighted. No BA timbre, very natural. Perfect amount of treble detail and air while allowing it to scale at higher volumes. Super smooth dynamics and incredible coherency. TOTL resolution, detail, layering, imaging, and staging. Bass is fine, but not a basshead set - still has a nice slam to it. 07 still scales better and more 3D, but CAD12 stage is more open and better tech. If you don't blast your brains out like me then this is it (although I'm not sure if they're selling this version - maybe request it specifically/ask Joseph?)

name: Thieaudio Valhalla
notes: TOTL all-rounder with "endgame" tech across the board, a better tuned U12T with better bass texture

name: Letshuoer Sonata
notes: TOTL balanced clean tonality with great detail and resolution. ESTs are well implemented - smooth but textured with good air. Could use more low-end and can get slightly bright depending on tips, but bass texture is great. No complaints. Endgame level across the board.

name: LETSHUOER Cadenza 12 2023/2024
notes: Retail version has more treble energy and less mid-bass vs pre-production tuning. Very airy and detailed, amazing layering, and one of the most resolving TOTL IEMs along with U12T.

name: Thieaudio V16 Divinity
notes: Musical baby

name: LETSHUOER MYSTIC 8
notes: Vocal benchmark for female vocals under $2000. Clean, airy, sweet, ethereal. Better than Diva and direct upgrade to OG Oracle and OG Mangird Tea. What the Braindamage and Cantor wishes they could be. Great technical performance, and scales decently well. Recommended listening volume is mid to high volume around 75-80dbs. Not for bassy libraries like hiphop, and can be a bit energetic on kpop/jpop/rock stuff with a lot of treble.

name: IO CIELO
notes: Endgame all-rounder tuning around $1000, very close to my all-rounder target. Great balance of detail, dynamics, and refinement - more transients and sharper attack than MK4, but also smoother than the more energetic Glacier. Basically zero issues with endgame performance across the board - maybe more sub-bass? And better scaling on more energetic tracks, but aside from that it's musical, technical, and versatile.

name: Sony-IER Z1R
notes: Best of the best in most areas, but vocals and mids can be thin due to fit issues. Insane bass texture/detail and HUGE soundstage. One of the best trebles I've heard.

name: Thieaudio Monarch MK4
notes: Smooth, clean, balanced, and slightly airy in the balance switch. Goes from a clean all-rounder to a warm/bassy all-rounder. Great tech. Basically a cheaper Prestige LTD with more tuning options. "Endgame" for most people, but the case is SHIT.

name: Thieaudio Prestige LTD
notes: Clean and natural signature with treble emphasis. LOTS of details with airy treble without going overboard (better treble extension vs MK2/MK3). Bass is not as impactful versus MK3 but has better separation. Overall a technical monster, but can be a bit dry due to less mid-bass. Vocals are further vs MK3 and MK2 (not as forward), giving it that open sense of space. MK2 still the best for vocals, but LTD is an endgame all-rounder.

name: Symphonium Crimson
notes: U-shaped/Slight V/W Shaped. Energetic treble. Great tech. Fun signature.

name: Thieaudio Prestige OG
notes: Sub-bass boost + treble boost. Similar to Crimson, lots of treble energy, great tech, more aggresive LTD.

name: FatFreq Grand Maestro
notes: The best basshead set. EXPENSIVE. If you just want bass HBB Punch way better value.

name: Kinera Imperial Loki
notes: Super clean and clear sound. Beautiful vocals. Everyhting is extremely well balanced. No special sauce tho.

name: Empire Ears Raven
notes: V/W Shaped. Energetic treble. Great tech. Fun bass and engaging signature. Overpriced?

name: Thieaudio Monarch MK2
notes: Neutral tuning with one of the clearest mid-ranges. Natural and clean vocals. Great resolution, separation, and detail. Can be a little dry with its analytical presentation. Bass is well-seperated from other instruments, but nothing special especially at $1K. Would've liked more depth, and treble is also a bit unstable and dips, resulting in a lack of air/depth. Mid-bass is just enough for my library, but would've liked more for genres like hiphop and rock. Cable is heavy, and fit may be too big for many (need to shove in deep).

name: Thieaudio Monarch MK3
notes: Better low-end texture and overall more engaging than MK2, but lacks the mid-range/vocal magic, so depending on your preference either is great. Still TOTL tech like MK2. Great all-rounder.

name: Elysian Apostle
notes: Clean, neutral, and clear vocals. Reminds me of a cleaner Volume S or slightly better OG Oracle, but very expensive, maybe if you can find one around $1000 since it's more of a sidegrade to RSV, Mystic 8, and Arcanis vocal wise. If you want clean vocals Monarch MK2 does the same thing but for $800 less.

name: Thieaudio Origin
notes: Best bassy set under $1K. Bassy/thicker meta tuning. You can actually feel the reverb and vibration from the bone conduction drivers, great control and low-end texture. Mids and treble are also well extended with no major issues, although it can get sharp at times with the snares/electronic stuff ie, past 3:30 on Time by Hikaru Utada.

name: Dunu Glacier
notes: Clean, balanced but engaging sound, clear vocals, great midrange and tech. Vocals can be a bit too forward/sharp. The most recent unit I got sounds different than the earlier ones which was bass-boosted diffuse field.

name: UM MEST MK2
notes: TOTL imaging chops/layering. Tons of micro-details. Great bass texture. Wide and 3D staging. Can be aggressive, and get fatiguing when cranked up/long-listening sessions.

name: UM MEST MK3
notes: A more neutral/slightly warm MEST MK2, less aggresive, easier to the ears, same technicalities. A little overpriced ngl.

name: UM MEST OG
notes: A MEST MK2 with slightly more uppermid/bass. More v-shaped. More AGGRESSIVE than MK2. Also gets fatiguing when cranked up/long-listening sesisons.

name: Symphonium Helios SE
notes: Best Treble around it's price. Super airy but still smooth. Bass-scoop isn't as bad as I thought, but those who want mid-bass - avoid it.

name: Thieaudio HYPE 10
notes: U-shaped, nice treble extention and dynamics, solid vocals, more low-end emphasis than MK3, dynamic and great all-rounder that doesn't specialize in anything.

name: XENNS TOP PRO
notes: Very technical, amazing resolution and detail for the price, treble is slightly crispy and sparkly, clean but dynamic all-rounder. Mid-volume set for the most part as treble can get hot at higher volumes. Easy rec, direct upgrade from Astrals.

name: XENNS Tea Pro SE
notes: Balanced all-rounder but still dynamic enough, natural timbre, treble is airy, and great tech for the price (around the same as Top Pro). Falls inbetween Hype 4 MK2 and Mega 7 in-terms of energy and dynamics. Cleaner and less bassy vs OG Tea Pro and a bump in detail and also smoother. Similar tuning to Top Pro but less vocal focused/sparkly, and more all-rounded/fuller. Great tech for the price. My unit graphs/sound different (less bass) than HBB's - you've been warned.

name: NICEHCK Rockies
notes: Balanced, clean, airy, with a slight treble emphasis, good EST implementation, great overall package and accesories at the price. Similar to TOP PRO but with ESTs and not as vocal centric. Easy rec if you want something balanced and airy.

name: AFUL Dawn-X
notes: Smooth treble, natural timbre, good sub-bass focused set, but transients can be a bit soft, and vocals are pulled back lacking final extension - non-fatiguing but not very engaging and "dynamic". A bassier 5+2 with smoother/more natural treble. Reminds me of the Luna but less mid-bass/vocals, more sub, and a little smoother. Bassy all-rounder like MK4 bass switch but with pulled back vocals, and less versatile since no switch option.

name: Thieaudio Monarch OG
notes: Endgame clarity and layering. Clean, clear, and balanced all-rounder sound. Great resolution, and open staging. Rumbly sub-bass but mid-bass tuck can kill some libraries and affect vocal thinness.

name: TangZu Xuan Wu Gate
rawName: TangZu Xuan Wu Gate ($650)  ($500 on sale)
notes: Clean, neutral, balanced, technical, laid back, very detailed. Neutral tuning done right while being a little dynamic/engaging. Tip wise Azla spinfits for more detail, tangzu sancai regular for smoother.

name: 64AUDIO U12T
notes: TOTL tech. Mid-scoop can affect mids/vocal texture and placement, recessed midrange, treble is harsh at high volumes. Great bass detail, but could have more impact.

name: Empire Ears EVO
notes: Great bass texture. BC driver actually works. Very well controlled but still impactful. Great resolution. Doesn't scale well because of spicy uppermids. Vocals often gets shouty on certain tracks, also overpriced asf imo

name: LETSHUOER Cadenza 12 2025
notes: Very technical bright leaning set, treble air is amazing, very detailed in the treble but also has lots of energy, can get fatiguing - treblehead set?

name: LETSHUOER EJ07
notes: TOTL mids. Most 3D and holographic staging yet. Imaging, separation, layering, and staging are all S level - only thing that's holding it back is the darker treble which can lead to softer notes vs, Diva, for example.The most immersive set for rock, alternative, ballads, and classical. An 07M that scales better with better staging. Great clarity and seperation. Treble is pushed back but still clear and evident in tracks (at higher volumes). Could use more low-end (but not an issue) and sharper note transients. Takes you on a journey. Needs to be listened to at high volume for the full effect.

name: Softears RSV OG
notes: Check the other RSV ranking below... But that aside, this unit has one of the best vocals I've heard on any IEM (especially for male artists). Mids and Treble is TOTL, smooth and well extended and has great naturalness and the perfect bite. Bass has great speed and still slams (even though it's BA? not rumbly), but stage and detail is average at it's price, but once it clicks with a track it's one of the most beautiful thing ever. Ran into distortion issues at high volume, but may be due to my source? (RSV too sensitive?)

name: Meze Astru
notes: Natural, immersive, full, with special sauce in the staging - decay has a prolonged reverb feeling to the stage/3D like. HIGH VOLUME LISTENING RECOMMENDED. Well-balanced, basically a fuller/thicker OG EJ07 - also reminds me of a sub-bass boosted OG MiM Dark Magician. Build is insanely sturdy and can withstand 4 tons of force on my hydraulic press without getting squashed. Only nitpick is the price since technical performance/micro details/imaging could be better, but I guess they can charge this much since it's the only one with this kind of staging and tonality on the market currently - got a premium tax on it - it is what it is.

name: IO Volare
notes: Best Harman IEM under $600 (my unit is less harman), smooth and natural, great layering and tech, bass texture could be better/not as good as Oracle MK3, but overall very balanced and great all-rounder, also, amazing unboxing and accessories

name: HiSenior MEGA5EST 7th
notes: New unit is better tuned/balanced, smooth, good all-rounder, and sounds like adjusted diffusefield.

name: 7th Acoustic Supernova
notes: Super smoooth. TOTL dynamics and treble air - dunno how they managed this airy and smooth with only BAs. Very clean, no sharpness, or sudden peaks, endgame separation and detail. Only drawback is that the sub-bass is a bit meh, and that the sound isn't that "unique". Very safe all-rounder, and one of the best under $1000. Endgame set. Aside from the bass, everything else is better than Monarch MK3, MK2 still has better vocals, but the Supernova beats them when it comes to treble extention and smootheness - too bad it's impossible to get one lol.

name: Thieaudio Oracle MK3
notes: Great bass texture, much better than predecessors, smooth and slightly airy giving it a sizzly timbre, great layering/separation, vocals are slightly laid back but not gone, very balanced across frequencies, monitor like, great all-rounder, and pretty safe - although not very dynamic and "fun". Azla clear tips gives a detail boost.

name: XENNS UP
rawName: XENNS UP ($699) with AZLA tips. Disc.
notes: Fast and clean bass but still rumbly and punchy. Beryllium DD baby. Well-seperated mids, and vocals still pop and aren't buried like other bass sets. Can use more treble extension (fixed with AZLA sedna tips).

name: EPZ 550
notes: Clean, clear, mid-range focused. Beautiful natural, open, and airy female vocals with slight bite to consonants. Reminds me of a fresh ocean breeze. Great vocals, reminds me of a more textured and detailed Oracle MK1. Great separation and layering. Low-end is lean and can get thin and sharp on certain tracks. Great for indie, ballads, acoustics, instrumentals, slower pop/R&B. Doesn't scale good on energetic genres due to the lean low-end and sharper transients - can get peaky on brighter songs. Not recommended for anything that needs low-end like hiphop, rap, rock. Nicher set for vocals.

name: Thieaudio Oracle OG
notes: Airy and relaxing vocals. Sweet and gentle presentation. Clean, clear vocals - could be too balanced and tame, could use better transients. Great separation, but stage size could be better.

name: Softears RSV MK2
notes: Bassy dynamic all-rounder with great low-end texture that slams hard with good note-weight/body. V-shape leaning and slight Hype 4 upgrade. Treble is smooth enouhg while holding dynamics, and vocals are well-tuned. Overall unboxing/accesories are great... just no ESTs at its price, I'd wait for sale.

name: Thieaudio Hype 4 MK2
notes: Clean, clear, smooth with airy treble emphasis/has the sauce, OCD pin point imaging, amazing detail retrieval and separation - punches way above its price point tech wise. Only downside is that treble can be too much on energetic genres like kpop/jpop/edm, and mid-bass could use more engagement for rock/bands - not a bassy set. Doesn't scale well, a mid-volume set that excels with certain genres like indie, acoustics, ballads, r&b, and slower pop stuff - recommended library playlist: https://music.apple.com/ca/playlist/hype-4-mk2/pl.u-55D6PmKiMZqGb9

name: Ziigaat Horizon
notes: Bright lean "Meta" inspired all-rounder, well-balanced, smooth, with great transients, and basically a slightly more detailed Astral with smoother treble and less sub-bass.Great details and tech for the price.

name: Binary EP321
notes: Clean, natural, balanced, but also still engaging and musical. Timbre is very realistic and treble is smooth enough while giving enough transients. Can get sharp at higher volumes. If you're looking for a chopin/daybreak upgrade these are it.

name: Yanyin Moonlight 2023
notes: Balanced, smooth, and clean presentation that scales beautifully with slightly forward/powerful vocals.

name: DUNU x Precogvision Mirai
notes: Bright leaning set with great tech. Clean mid-range, sharp imaging, sparkly female vocals with decent amount of air. Does get fatiguing and sharp on more energetic tracks and genres like EDM/POP/KPOP/JPOP, aka lower to mid volume set. Sounds very good on slower genres like indie, acoustics, ballads - adds more energy and liveliness to the slower nature of those genres. Mid-bass is lacking and would not recommend for rock or hiphop.

name: Softears Karma
notes: Clean, clear, neutral-vocal leaning tuning with basically no low-end. Great layering, separation, imaging, and detail... however vocals can sound thin and too light due to the rolled off bass, and if you need low-end - forget it. Very niche iem for instrumentals or vocal ballads that has no low-end elements. Also costs way too much, and the unboxing is lowkey a scam at that price. Both the Perseus and CKLVX would be better value wise.

name: ZIIGAAT Arcanis
notes: My favourite vocals under $500 (best imo). A more refined OG Mangird Tea with better resolution and tech. Has the "sauce" in the treble with slight bite/sizzle that adds dynamic contrast to vocal consonants. Recommend listening at higher volumes on slower vocal centric tracks. Don't rec hiphop or genres that needs lots of sub-bass. Can get spicy with kpop/jpop at higher volumes/don't rec blasting with more energetic tracks. Pin point imaging and open staging, good for gaming.

name: MiM Dark Magician OG
notes: Weighted and airy vocals but with expansive staging. 3D/ball imaging. Coherency and dynamics are TOTL. Clear - details are "big"/forward, but can use better separation. Super immersive. Could use more sub-bass and resolution.

name: Yanyin Carmen
notes: An OG EJ07 that does vocal scaling. A blast your brains out kinda set. Full, powerful, extended, VERY forward vocals, might be too much for some people. Reveals every last bit of emotion from the artist's voice. Makes the song very intimate and vulnerable. VERY genre depedent, check playlist in the video description. It's basically an RSV that scales at high volume. Super immersive, great centre-imaging (or as good as it gets in an IEM), and mid-bass quality competes with the MMK3 and others. Treble is dark, not for trebleheads or people who like air. Detail takes a hit, and stage is very close, like the artist is singing right infront of you. A truly unique experience, but again, it's gonna be a hit or miss for many people depending on their library and how loud they listen - NOT a mid-lower volume set... and it comes with a $2 pouch at $850 LOL, but hey, I mean they actually get away with it because when it hits, it HITS.

name: Softears Twilight
notes: Slightly warm/neutral, very well balanced, good scaling, TOTL male vocals, big staging, wait for sale

name: ZIIGAAT Luna
notes: Airy, smooth, warm, laid-back, balanced, lush and dreamy vibes. Great for rock/metal, scales decently high. Mid-bass over sub. Not as vocal forward as Arcanis and other vocal sets. My Luna graphs very different than HBB's - wait for more reviews.

name: Xenns Mangird Tea OG
notes: Discontinued, but one of the best female vocals I've heard on any IEMs at higher volume. Top tier mids under $500. Spring Tips improves vocals and treble clarity. Great around the head imaging, but imaging is less layered than 07M. Treble can be dark at lower/mid volumes, but shines when cranked up. Super immersive. High volume listening recommened.

name: LETSHUOER EJ07M
notes: Holographic staging with an amazing midrange. Great bass texture and impact. Incredibly immersive and endgame for most. Has more sub-bass and treble air than OG doesn't scale as well.

name: Thieaudio HYPE 4
notes: One of the best all-rounders under $600 (v-shaped harman). Treble quality is smooth and well extended. Great low-end texture with lots of impact. Good vocals. Solid tech, and just solid in general.

name: XENNS Tea Pro
notes: A more resolving Davinci, literally. The Tea magic is gone :( but it's now the most refined and well-balanced. It's the most bassy one with better low-end texture, heavier notes, more details, better resolution, and the better all-rounder pick. Also bassy balanced like the Hype 4, both are just as good to me, and comes down to what I'm feeling that day

name: Softears RSV MK1 no-unit variance
notes: Clean, balanced, full, natural, uppermids/vocal emphasis. Still a mid-range set, but vocals don't pop as much as the RSV I originally got, aka not as saucy. Recent unit is still a good balanced vocal set for male vocals, but not as special and very pricey, maybe on sale. This is the RSV MK1 tuning most people will get... guess I got a rare 1 of 1 lol.

name: Elysian Pilgrim Noir
notes: Good but expensive. Recommended if you can find it for around $500. Direct upgrade to the AFUL Explorer. Scales great. Reminds me of the EJ07M but a bit smoother and less dynamic. Prefer it more than the OG pilgrim, but definitely not worth $400 more lol.

name: Symphonium Titan
notes: Most balanced bass set I've heard so far without sacrificing the fun/texture/impact in the low-end. Open staging, full sounding, deep sub-bass, vocals aren't buried either. No big peaky treble, good extension. No real issues aside from the price maybe. A very unique bass experience since usually the low-end overtakes the other fr, but with the Titan you can hear everything while having that impactful/authoritative bass.

name: Kiwi Ears Astral
notes: Great all-rounder. Slighty airy with good sub-bass extenion. Balanced but still fun. A cleaner, airier, and less sharp/sparkly version of the Meta/Crescent - vocals pop out more. Tip rec Sancai regular or Softears Ultra clears. Treble peak can get sharp with certain units (mine was fine).

name: Softears Studio 4
notes: "Correct" and neutral tuning. Natural vocals, not as forward like RSV but zero faults. Slight Improvement over RSV in-terms of seapration and stage size/treble is same/not as warm.

name: ORIVETI OH700VB
notes: Replaced by Astral. A more engaging Supernova, cleaner, with better sub-bass, and vocals. Very big stage and fantastic separation and layering. Vocals are airy without being too sharp. Lots of air/reminds me of the LTD. Mid-bass scoop can affect some libraries like HIPHOP and EDM, but perfect for indie/ballads/acoustics/intrumentals and slower songs.

name: ZIIGAAT Crescent
notes: Slightly warm, full, and sparkly/crispy treble. A warmer TOP PRO with a step down in technical performance. Treble can get much on kpop/jpop/energetic tracks. Mid-volume set, doesn't scale as well as Odyssey but has better tech.

name: YU9 Que
notes: Smooth listen, non-fatiguing, balanced and leans towards mids/neutral, scales good, full, natural, but lacks dynamics/transients and vocal extension. Reminds me of the OG SA6 with a little more treble and low-end, but less mids, and even more pulled back vocals... Similar to the Meta tunings, reminds me of a more neutral Astral/Crescent/Horizon - Good, but a bit overhyped and priced a bit high for a 1DD+3BA, tech is slightly behind the Astrals and should be under $300 imo.

name: Softears Volume S
notes: Amazing vocals under $500 with the stock switch/clear tips or tangzu sancai regular (no impedance boost) with amazing vocal scaling. Recommended for higher volume listening like ballads, slower indie/bands. Better than Studio 4 vocal wise, but Studio 4 is the better all-rounder. Volume S is more mid/vocal centric than Studio 4, and more immersive and "musical". Other switch configuration offers more clarity and detail at the cost of scaling with uppermids/treble boost (cleaner harman 2019/better at mid-volume). Stock switch tuning can also be neutral and relaxing if you don't crank it up, and overall Volume S has good variety and differentiates itself with the different tunings. Also, well implemented BAs. Passive Radiator effect is questionable.

name: Symphonium Meteor
notes: Meaty textured mid-bass, but can be a bit much. VVery warm sound. Library dependent. Airy treble, but vocals are a bit pushed back and buried.

name: Kiwi Ears x HBB PUNCH
notes: Endgame "balanced-basshead" set. Amazing low-end texutre, rumble, reverb, slam, and more bass than Origin and Titan - goes harder than those. Vocals and treble also still well extended, not congested, or cramped staging. Good balance while giving amazing fun bass. Recommend Azla Sedna light blue tips for more air, or Divinus Velvets. EQ down -3dbs at 250hz, low-shelf, 0.5 Q, and you'll get the Endgame IE target (my all-rounder target).

name: Punch Audio Martilo
notes: Cheaper, and slightly more energetic HBB Punch with slightly less mid-bass and slam. Endgame "balanced" basshead. Imaging feels sharper than Punch, but treble is not as smooth, aside from that very similar tech and low-end.

name: EPZ K9
notes: All-rounder with slight v-shape tonality. EW300 upgrade. Natural and sweet vocals, nice mid-bass slam, treble is nicely extended, well-balanced with a mix of smoothness and contrast, and great packaging and design.

name: SIMGOT EM10
notes: A more immersive version of the Pilgrim with better mid-bass kick. More airy and slightly more detailed in the treble. Harman vocal gain might be too much for some. Bass might be boomy depending on the tips. Use Tangzu Sancai tips (regular)

name: XENNS TOP
notes: What the Variations should've been. Fantastic tehcnincalities. Neutral-bright leaning. Nothing wrong with it at mid-volume, but I can see treble can be too much at highet volumes.

name: TangZu Bajie
notes: Clean/balanced meta tuning with sharp imaging and transients - an edgier take on the meta tuning, more dynamic. Has great potential for EQ due to its bigger 14.2MM bass. Low-end is more prominent than the graph suggest, great bass texture and impact, although the bone conduction driver is more subtle vs the Origin. Clear sound with great separation, can run into some peaks around 5K, and tonality has more bite vs smooth but not overly sharp or jarring.

name: Dunu SA6 ULTRA
notes: An SA6 with improvement in treble extension, and stage air; better tuned Oracle2 with wider stage. Relaxing tonality but also very resolving. Airy stage with great depth and height. Smooth dynamics and great coherency. Realistic timbre. Great detail and clarity. Mids and vocals may not be forward enough for some genres. Low-end is quick and has great separation form mids but lacks rumble and slam. Tuning A+ to S- depending on your library.

name: HiSenior MEGA7
notes: Clean, balanced, smooth, neutral leaning, in-offensive, good tech, everything is "fine"... a little more dynamic than Dunu 242. Sounds like the earlier units of the MEGA5ESTs. Could use more dynamics and transients, and not very musical. Basically a less vibrant/engaging Top Pro/Tea Pro SE with less detail. Smooth listen for those who want something relaxing, but lots of better options for cheaper like Orch 2, Canon Pro, Que. Doesn't have the treble sauce like the H4 MK2, Top Pro, Rockies - wait for sale.

name: Kiwiears Orchestra 2
notes: Clean, clear, balanced, great layering/separation, neutral, vanilla + with slight pop in the vocals, best orchestra to date. Well priced with nice accessories - just not for bass lovers. Low-end impact/rumble can feel light with drums and guitars.

name: Yanyin Canon Pro
notes: Clean, neutral, balanced. Airy treble but smooth, great tech. Recommend UP UP switch with bass boost. A smoother pilgrim basically.

name: CrinEar Meta
notes: Bright-leaning all-rounder with sparkly treble sauce. Great tech for price and great accessories. Good coloration that's not vanilla and safe as other crin collabs. Can be fatiguing at higher volumes, tip dependent, rec sancai wide/regular or Softear Ultra Clear/EPZ clear tips.

name: EPZ 530
notes: Great set for jazz/blues/soul/acoustic. Thick and lush. Warm but with nice treble extension. Solid tech. Vocals can be overly husky and buried in busier songs.

name: Elysian Pilgrim
notes: Clean, clear, all-rounder, similar tuning as the Dusk but with better vocals, bass quality is great as well, aethestically pleasing too. If you want a clean all-rounder, or sensitive in the 3-8K, these are great.

name: Dunu SA6
notes: Gorgeous mid range and great dynamics. Good timbre makes me forget it's a full BA set. Good bass texture, but wish it had more rumble. Wish stage and imaging was more 3D. Could use more treble air and staging. Relaxed listening vs 07M's immersion.

name: Moondrop Illustrious
notes: Basically the Softears Twilight with less sub-bass extension, alot more neutral and monitor like, and very pricy since Twilight goes on sale for $700 with a more musical playback. This is just neutral.

name: Effect Audio Perseus
notes: Clean balanced sound that's slighlty mid-range leaning with clear, detailed vocals and sharp transients/attack. Bass is punchy even though it doesnt graph as much with great separation and pull/push. "Endgame" level separation and tech but can be bass light especially in the mid-bass slam and overall weight/fullness. Treble is on the sparklier side and has that slight edge to them instead of being airy and smooth, which means scaling wise it can get sharp at higher volumes, aka this is a mid/high-volume set most of the time. Also a bit pricy for the driver config, but build and accessories are definetly premium and top notch.

name: NICEHCK NX8 TI
notes: Clean, balanced, airy, technical, slight pop/sharpness to the attack and imaging, essentially a mini NICEHCK ROCKIES but without the smoother EST treble - same tech but $100 less... however bass is light, vocals are more pushed back, and overall not that dynamic and lacks some contrast. Good value overall if you just want detail.

name: TangZu Tian Peng
notes: A cleaner more neutral Bajie with less bass and more treble energy. Clean, slightly vocal forward with some bite. Azla tips for more bass and treble energy/bite but can get shouty - Sancai Nobles for a smoother/neutral/montior like sound. Great tech, but wish it had ESTs like its competition.

name: Effect GAEA
notes: Super aggresive, exciting, v-shape, treblehead. Low-end is also very punchy and rumbly. TOTL technical performance with tons of details and OCD, but gets fatiguing. Shouty.

name: Moondrop Variations
notes: Very clear with lots of detail. Sub-bass has a nice rumble and texture. Amazing treble extension and stage air. Female vocals are vibrant and shines. Mid-bass cut is real, affecting some genres and male vocals. Note-weight can be light.

name: Sennheiser IE600
notes: Tons of detail and amazing clarity. Stage is smaller than most IEMs at/below its price tag but very well defined details and imaging within that space. Bass is detailed, but amount is not as much as graph would suggest. Treble gets sharp and fatiguing at longer-listening/higher volumes. Stage can feel cramped.

name: Aur Neon Pro
notes: Slightly edgier Supernova with punchier low-end. Not as smooth and refined, but more engaging.

name: Dunu SA6 MK2
notes: V-shaped SA6 Ultra with more recessed mids and vocals. Sharper and more bass than SA6U but mids are buried in busier tracks.

name: ZIIGAAT Odyssey
notes: A warm/mini Subtonic Storm that scales better and fuller with less tech. A musical odyssey. High volume set, great scaling, a cleaner/midrange focused Explorer with better layering and detail. Takes you on a journey like the OG EJ07. Bass is thumpy and rumbly at higher volumes, vocals are clean and balanced with slight treble emphasis, and very immserive. Highly recommended for slow-rock, indie/alternative, ballads, fits my preference to a T.

name: 7th Acoustic x QoA RYUSEI Vocal Rank
rawName: 7th Acoustic x QoA RYUSEI ($129)   Vocal Rank
notes: Vocal specific rank. Natural, extended, clear, and detailed vocals with slight shine and sparkle in the endnotes. Has the "sauce" for female vocals and excels on slower genres that allows the artist to be in focus. Feels like I'm getting hit by a ray of light like the RSV, but not as forward and full but has more glimmer and shimmer in the attack of the treble. Lots of mico-nuances from the artists' breathe and lingering notes and creates a sense of intimacy other balanced vocal sets don't offer. One of, if not the best female vocals under $350 - incredible value for vocals. The cable is also sick for $80. Only nitpick would be the bass texture could be better with more weight/slam, and that the treble can get fatiguing with kpop/jpop energetic genres (which I don't recommend listening to with these anyways).

name: Softears Edge
notes: Saw the graph and thought was going to be another muddy bassy set, but was happily surprised by the resolution, stage, and smooth extended treble. Very good for rock/hiphop/metal since the uppermids are tame in the vocals but still has an open feeling to the sound. Instrument separation is surprisingly decent given the amount of bass boost, it's not not muddy, or overly warm and soft in the texture. It's not going to be technical like the Tea Pros, or airy like the Meteors, but it doesn't feel closed in or congested and the bass texture is VERY GOOD. Meaty, tactile, thick, great feeling of push and pull to the driver, heavy in the slam - basically all the buzzwords and things a bass lover would want. The main issue would be the $500 asking price and the pushed back vocals. If you can find these on sale around $350, and love bass and don't mind tamer vocals - go for it, it'll be my guilty pleasure once in a while when I want to slam my brains out.

name: Letshuoer x Effect Ember
notes: Direct upgrade to the Aful Explorers - better bass texture/slam and treble extension. High volume set as vocals and midrange will be too recessed without scaling, but very immersive like the Explorers... just that price is very high for single planar.

name: Crinear Monolith
notes: Thick and heavy mid-bass slam with textured low-end presentation - got the mid-bass sauce. Satisfying basshead listen at higher volumes, and scales very well due to overall smoothness in the treble and uppermids. Vocals still have enough clarity and are huskier on male artists - not much bleed into the mids. Treble is smooth, but lacks the nuance and micro details in the air and resolution. Technical performance is enough, but doesn't punch its asking price… basically, it's easy to love, but hard to recommend due to the gold tax and overall price.

name: Kinera Phoenixcall 2.0
notes: Bassy refined v-shape sound with great low-end texture on par with odyssey and astralis - essentially a more v-shaped OG Odyssey. Vibrant, great dynamic constrast, and engaging. Treble can get too bright on energetic songs, but overall much better than OG Phoenixcall.

name: Yanyin Baker
notes: Slightly warm leaning with tingly treble presentation. Full, and great for male vocals, basically the Arcanis with more bass but doesn't treble is not as smooth and doesn't scale as well. Vocals are not as clean and emphasized, but better low-end.

name: Xenns Mangird Tea 2
notes: Slightly more technical version of the OG TEAs. Thumpier low end, and treble is more extended. Less forward presentation. Stage has more depth. Can't scale as well as OG. Vocals are not as "magical" as OG.

name: Softears SE6 LIVE
notes: Smooth, warm/dark, natural, full, mid-bass leaning, scales great... but needs volume or it sounds dead/low-fidelity at lower volumes - it's also 3x more than it should be since it's basically a warmer/darker Crinear Reference with similar performance.

name: Simgot EA1000 non-bright unit
notes: Bright-leaning with the best bass texture at its price point, and one of the best under $500. Incredible resolution and clarity with stunning female vocals. Timbre is as natural as you can get given its price. There is some masking in the vocals just like most IEMs with a 1.5-2K peak, and treble does get too energetic with certain genres like KPOP/EDM. However, mesh filters+gold nozzle fixes this for the most part.

name: ZIIGAAT CINCOTRES
notes: Great bass texture, vocals, treble, solid all-rounder. Similar to Variations but with a smaller/delayed scoop, more mid-bass, but not as much treble/air. A fun bassy sound but still well-balanced. Correct polarity.

name: Gizaudio CHOPIN on sale
notes: If Harman wasn't boring and had a few drinks

name: 7Hz Timeless 2
notes: Good all-rounder set with solid tech. Good variety with the nozzles that actually changes the sound. Treble is smoother than other planars, and not much "planar timbre".

name: Thieaudio Hype 2
notes: Mini-Monarch MK3 with less bass and details. 80% there. Harmanish tuning, and best all-rounder before Studio 4.

name: Letshuoer Cadenza 4
notes: Slightly bright, clean sound, very airy, sweet vocals. Great separation and resolution. Reminds me of the OG Orcales. Follows Harman 2019 but with more air. Needs more low-end, not an all-rounder. Not rec for hiphop, kpop, rock. Very good for indie, ballads, classical and acoustics.

name: Yanyin HBB Mahina
notes: Warm and intimate signature. Vocals are very forward but lacks treble air. Needs scaling.

name: MYER CKLVX D62 Sancai Wides
notes: Very good all-rounder set with great dynamics on top. Stage is wide with great technical performance. Vocals pop out just enough, bass is tactile with good slam, overall a solid set if you want a more engaging set that does everything very well. Only downside is that it can be a bit sharp with stock tips - highly recommend TangZu Sancai Wide tips, helps smoothens out and open the sound - mandatory for max potential

name: MYER SL224
notes: Same tuning as the EPZ P50 but fancier with a little more sub-bass, and slightly more detailed in the treble but barely noticeable. This is "technically" better, but P50 would be the better value since you can get it for around $160 on sale.

name: Tanchjim Kaiser
notes: Clean, balanced, smooth, natural and airy. Very good all-rounder that's slighlty mid-range/vocal leaning. Great layering/resolution for price, and snappy bass decay - although could use more impact/rumble for bass lovers. Better than Soda imo with more treble air and less smoothed out.

name: TangZu HE Zhang Liao
notes: Warm leaning flat high scaling sound. Immersive, full, natural with linear mid-bass glide and tame 2-4K. A more balanced/technical AFUL EXPLORER.

name: ZIIGAAT ODYSSEY 2
notes: Balanced all-rounder with a slight vocal/mid-centric presentation. Vocal scaler. Snappy/punchy/tight bass. A cleaner, smoother, and more mid-centric Odyssey aka no more bass sauce and bite. Rec with higher volume for full potential.

name: CrinEar Reference
notes: Smooth, neutral, natural vocals that scales great. Not dead boring due to its ability to scale vocals. Recommended for high volume listening, and good for energetic genres like kpop/jpop. Details could be better for price, and not much sub-bass quantity/rumble - wait for sale.

name: Juzear Harrier
notes: Smooth, non-faitguing, mid-range focused sound with sub-bass boost, scales great. Strings and woodwind instruments pop out and are highlighted clearly. Bass comes out when it needs to, full enough to sound natural. Basically a less tehcnical Que that's more sub-bass focused, and without the premium build and packaging. Tech could be better for the price as lots of other IEMs around its price will out compete it, as well as cheaper ones. Overall nicely tuned, but a bit pricey - wait for sale.

name: EPZ P50 on sale
notes: Clean balanced tuning done right. A better tuned MEGA5EST & MOONDROP Meteor with fuller low-end, and more treble extension, same tech, but more dynamic - also half the price. A Mega5EST with better vocals and dynamics but less smooth and airy. Low-end will be weak to some people and on certain tracks. Not the most unique sound since it's clean/neutral/balanced.

name: BINARY 1900
notes: Balanced all-rounder with good texture and detail. Good if you want a balanced listen but not very unique or different, kinda reminds me of a less shouty Harman 2019. Similar to the YU9 QUE but doesn't have the scaling/sauce and slightly more v-shaped. I'd go EP321 if you want a cleaner sound since it's got the MEMS treble sauce and more detail up top.

name: Meze Alba 2025 Unit
notes: Very smooth, natural, clean, well-balanced all-rounder, great for EQ. One of the most comfy IEMs I've tried. Could use more Dynamics/transients and details. Good build, looks clean. Recent unit I got might be slightly different in the treble than older models, but yours may vary. Like it more than Daybreak as a smooth/clean set.

name: CrinEar DayBreak
notes: Balanced smooth all-rounder. Safe and inoffensive. Here we go again. Very similar tuning as P50 and SL224. Less vocal centric vs P50s, but more bassy and all-rounded. Slightly slightly less technical than SL224.

name: FlipEars LEGION
notes: Fun and bassy, v-shape, great low-end slam and texture, full, rumbly, solid tech imaging, and cool faceplate... but price is a bit high.

name: MYER SLIIVO SL41 MK1
notes: Solid all-rounder for those who like a slightly warm dynamic listen with good transients and imaging - a more contrasty and fuller version of the Daybreak.

name: Letshuoer Astralis
notes: Sub-bass boosted all-rounder, very dynamic, engaging, and vibrant with great musical contrast. Great bass texture with good imaging and slight zing in the transients. Well-extended, non congested, but still bassy.

name: ZIIGAAT LUSH
notes: A cleaner more technical AFUL Explorer with a more open sense of space and airier treble. High volume set. Very smooth and balanced at higher scaling - has a "Lush" and full sound. Mid-volume sounds kinda anemic and too inoffensive, wouldn't rec at lower volumes unless you're using as background music while working, but very immersive with scaling like the Odyssey, but less v and more chill.

name: ZIIGAAT DOSCINCO
notes: Benchmark bass set before the UP. Low-end is impactful, rumbly, heavy, and slams hard with reverb detail. Ideal for hiphop/rap/r&b/rock. Separation & resolution not the best around its price, but enough for what it's going for.

name: Kiwi Ears Orchestra Lite old unit
rawName: Kiwi Ears Orchestra Lite ($250) old unit
notes: Great vocals. Clean and neutral signature. A bit vanilla and "boring" but scales great with volume.

name: Hisenior MEGA5 EST BASS
notes: The Mega5est 7th but with more sub-bass. That's it. Does sound better now, more "musical" and less vanilla and boring. A good comforting and smooth listen that scales well. Bass texture isn't as good as Tea Pro, Hype 4, Estrella tho. Similar to 61T, a bit smooth in the bass, but a better version of it in the timbre and vocals/treble. ESTs are not obvious but more subtle while being well-balanced in the mids and treble.

name: Seeaudio Yume OG
notes: Vocal benchmark along with EPZ P50 until Volume S, OG Oracles and RSV for most - natural and open vocals. Midranged focus, can use better bass texture and treble extension.

name: Dunu x Gizaudio Davinci
notes: Warm leaning with thick, thumpy mid-bass that hits pretty deep and hard. Decent vocal and treble extension, although female vocals are warmer and huskier. Good for hiphop, rap, r&b, but low-end isn't fast enough for busier genres like rock for example. Bass texture and resolution is slightly soft and not very separated, hits really hard, but sometimes bass notes feels like they've mushed together into one note. Hype 4 is straight up a better version of the Davinci when it comes to low-end texture and separation, as well as overall resolution and vocal playback; and if you're ok with EQing the Hype 2's low-end those are better as well because they use the same isobaric design as the 4s (Low-shelf, 100hz, +2-3db, Q 0.5)

name: ZIIGAAT x HBB Arcadia
notes: Niche/high volume set. Great scaling, warm, bassy, thick, comforting listen. A mini MEGA5EST Bass. Initmate and immersive experience. Not the most technical for the price, and vocals can be a bit too husky.

name: Kiwi Ears KE4
notes: Just get Odyssey it's better. Warm/bassy with solid vocal and treble extension (not buried) that scales really well with good treble air to not sound too intimate. Has a fuller noteweight with one of the best low-ends under $200. Recommended to be listened at higher volumes. A mid-volume version of the Explorer, bassier, and more open.

name: Moondrop x Crinacle DUSK 2nd Unit
notes: Fills in the uppermids, better extension, less 8-10K peak, less channel imbalance, and just a better tuning overall versus the first unit - that's chifi qc baby!!

name: KiwiEars Septet
notes: Bright-leaning with slight warmness - has an unique sparkly/lush, airy, and spacious sound. Great tech for the price, treble is not overly harsh or peaky (at mid volume), pretty smooth with the extra mid-bass balancing out the treble boost. Vocals are pushed back/not fully extended and not as prominent. Mid-volume set, doesn't scale well. Gets spicy with energetic genres past mid-volume. Great for instrumentals, acoustics, indie, classical, etc.

name: Hisenior MEGA5EST 7th old unit
notes: Neutral, clean, well-balanced, monitor like, great tech, but boring. Just get the TOP PRO, Oracle MK3 or Volare, or Xuan Wu Gate.

name: SIMGOT SUPERMIX4
notes: Endgame Harman, very technical for price, slight treble pop with a brittle/bite to the notes, fun dynamics with the treble + bass, recent units have more sub-bass. Great value. Some units might be hotter in the treble/pzt timbre

name: EPZ P40
notes: Bright leaning smooth balanced tonality like the EM6L but with a little better resolution. Very good for EQ since it's smooth, but can be too bright stock. Good tech for the price and has great EQ potential.

name: AAV CJ20
notes: A smoother and airier version of the OG S12. Bright leaning all-rounder with good sub-bass rumble. Might be too bright for some like the OG S12s, but very good for metal due to airy treble along with great tech.

name: Hidizs MP145 Pro
notes: Clean, balanced, vocal focused tonality with slight sparkle in the end notes. Sounds like a more resolving and detailed EA1000s with less low-end. Pin point imaging with quick transients. Might be too lean and sharp on more energetic genres, but very nice for vocals.

name: Kiwi Ears Quintet
notes: Great tech and treble detail. Balanced all-rounder. Solid performance to price value, but metallic timbre and treble peak can be an issue.

name: Moondrop Meteor
notes: Neutral, clean and clear vocals, vocals pop out, good tech. Next to no planar timbre - one of the least planar like planars. Treble isn't sizzly and bright, but vocals can get shouty on energetic tracks, and doesn't scale very well. Bass is not that impactful and textured, can be a bit too pushed back in the mix. A bit too vanila like the Mega5EST, but just with more vocal emphasis now and less smooth in the treble. NO ESTS for whatever reasons, makes it less airy and smooth compared to sets with ESTs. Both Volare and Variations would still be better, and EPZ P50 is just a better tuned and cheaper version of the Meteor.

name: Moondrop x Crinacle Silicon
notes: Clean, clear, balanced, full low-end, sharp/quick attack, good texture and detail. MEMS is well controlled and no timbre issues for the MOST PART, but treble can sound hard/brittle/PZT like on certain energetic tracks, and not as airy/refined vs knowles/sonion BAs or good MP. A better textued/detailed Daybreak that's more mid-range focused, but at the cost of timbre, air, and smoothness. For most people the Daybreaks/P50 would still be better value as they're both ~$100 cheaper and more natural sounding.

name: Truthear NOVA
notes: NEED FOAM TIPS makes the treble smooth and clear. Very clean harman sound with smooth but well extended treble/one of the best treble under $200, no roll-off. The pinnacle of trying not to offend anyone, but light bass/low-end; another harman.

name: Kiwiears Halcyon
notes: Sub-bass boosted all-rounder with great treble extension and "bouncy" sub-woofer like sub-bass. MEMS is well-implemented with no graininess timbre, smooth enough while maintaining transients. Versatile and engaging. Vocals could be more powerful and better extended, can get peaky at high volume (80dbs), and sounds thin and too bright with kpop/jpop. Lack of lower-mids can also be an issue for certain tracks. Update: Has weird high-pitched artifact sound/noise floor from the mems? Unit may be broken.

name: Dunu Vulkan 2 Maybe at -250
notes: Neutral/vocal centric set with very little sub-bass. A very "unique" tuning for a neutral sound. Very genre dependent. Clean and clear vocals with a slight bite. Lower-mids are just enough to bring enough note-weight and body. Not recommended for anything that needs sub-bass like hiphop, rap, EDM, and some POP songs. Recommend listening volume past 70dbs with indie, ballads, acoustics, slow rock.

name: Juzear Lightshuttle
notes: All-rounder with good tech and slight MP sizzle in upper treble. Basically the daybreak but less mid-bass and not as smooth. Adjusted Harman 2019 with less vocal shout and fuller lower mids. Does the job, but nothing special, and a bit pricy vs Supermix4 and Daybreaks. Wait for sale if you really want it.

name: Tanchjim Soda Maybe at -250
notes: Balanced, smooth, laid back, neutral leaning like the fission and origin but with more sub-bass extension and rumble and slightly more resolving. Not the best value since tuning is very similar as the fission which is half its price.

name: Kiwiears Aether
notes: Clean, balanced, with slight air boost in the treble. Bass sounds like a DD with great texture. Cheaper better tuned P5+2. Not as smooth as Timeless 2 with more dynamic contrast with a slight sizzle from the treble boost. Good value for a planar.

name: Binary Dynaquattro
notes: Natural vocals, good treble extension, bass is tight and more resolving vs 61t and Davinci. Overall very well balanced and clean. There are some small peaks at 8-10k and 15-20K which can be an issue on some songs, and there is masking around 4-8k region, but overall, solid all-rounder.

name: MYER CK2V
notes: A better tuned version of the Braindance for 2x less. Fuller, less sizzle and artifical, better timbre, vocals are clearer. Still have slight planar sizzle but in a balanced way. Good pick if you want something neutral/bright.

name: MYER SLIIVO SL41 PRO
notes: All-rounder with sharp transients/attack, resolving, detailed, and has a nice contrast. Gets a bit peaky in the uppermids on more energetic kpop/jpop, mid-bass/male vocals could use more weight/fullness. Basically a more technical OG SL41 at the cost of weight and smoothness. Perfect energy at mid-volume but wouldn't recommend for higher listening/scaling due to the uppermids boost peaks.

name: Simgot ET142 New Nozzles
notes: Lots of variety with nozzles.Tames down 2K, keeps treble extension, basically a Timeless 2 with better fit and more detail with blue nozzle.

name: Dunu 142
notes: Meta tuning very similar to Astral but vocals/treble are boosted more and less mid-bass. Good tech, but balance is off now and can get a bit sharp. I'd still go Astral, basically same sound but more natural and less sharp.

name: SIVGA Nightingale
notes: LESS-TREBLE UNIT. VERY GENRE SPECIFIC. Listen at HIGH VOLUME with slower tracks (slow rock, ballads, indie, jazz, blues, acoustics, instrumentals etc). TOTL stage (airy+reverb), layering, treble detail, but vocals and sub-bass are rolled-off/pushed back, losing details there otherwise would be at least be S- for tech. Treble can also be too energetic depending on the unit (a lot of them graph with lots of treble - mine doesn't sound that boosted), so in-general NOT RECOMMENDED for libraries with a lot of sub-bass (rolled-off) or energy (too sharp if you get a boosted unit). That aside, gives me OG EJ07 vibes immersion wise. Hard to recommend because unit variations.

name: SIVGA Nightingale Pro
notes: Neutral bright leaning with sparkly treble and airy extension. Clean and clear sound, good separation and imaging... only issue is that it has literally no sub-bass and very lean mid-bass. Does not work for many genres except maybe acoustics, ballads, indie etc. Has more vocal boost than OG. Very niche set, pass for most people.

name: Moondrop X Crinacle DUSK
notes: Inoffensive safe tuning, less fatiguing uppermids good for jpop/kpop. Vocals lack the last bit of extension, detail, and power. DSP APP is a shit show. Heavy competition from Nova, Cincotres, Hype 4.

name: Aful Performer 8S Maybe at -300
notes: Neutral laid back with treble bite/emphasis. Basically the P8 but with more sub-bass. Vocals are too recessed at mid/lower volumes but can't scale high enough due to treble having too much bite and slight metallic timbre. If you want balanced tonality just get EP321 better in every aspect and for cheaper. 5+2 would be better for a more balanced sound.

name: AFUL Performer 8 Maybe at -300
notes: Good neutral set. Airy and open staging but with forward vocals although lacking in extension. Great layering and details but not 3D and more flat. Vocals could also be more open, and feels "stuck".

name: JUZEAR 81T
notes: Clean balanced sound with good punch low-end, but... Harman 2019, just get Supermix 4 or Nova.

name: HiSenior Cano Cristales
notes: Exciting v-shape, graphs and sounds like a more aggressive/sharper Estrella that's less smooth/refined and more peaky. Uppermids can get shouty and fatiguing. Needs some sonions to smooth things out. Maybe at $250-300 with Sancai tips.

name: Moondrop Blessing 3
notes: Bright-neutral. Slight resolution bump over the B2 Dusk, but at the cost of weak bass and sharp 6K.

name: Night Oblivion Butastur
notes: Overpriced as hell - I don't get the hype. Vocals are way too shouty with masking. Treble peaks around 10K with a dip in the air afterwards. Low-end is "good", but nothing amazing for the price. Detail retrieval and separation is competitive, but that's pretty much it. If you want a clean sound there are ALOT of other options for better like even the Blessing 3.

name: MYER CKLVX Lava
notes: Balanced, mid-range focused, neutral sound. Very technical with great treble extension that is also smooth. Great technical value for the price, but there is a noticeable bass roll-off - again, neutral leaning. Can sound thin and light and lacking dynamics for genres like pop/hiphop/r&b/edm - basically anything that needs some bass... Can also get fatiguing due to the uppermids/treble focus without enough fullness. However, if you can overlook the lack of bass quanitity, and have a library like vocal ballads/indies/slower tracks then these are a great value performance wise with a smooth clean sound.

name: FATFREQ x EA QUANTUM
notes: Bright and full sound, very detailed, sparkly, airy, tons of treble extenstion... but it gets fatiguing with the stock filters. Blue filter has the best balance but still doesn't scale too well. 300 mesh filter goes hard tho - check modded ranking at bottom.

name: AFUL Cantor
notes: LOW VOLUME SET. Clean, airy, and highly resolving at its price with endgame separation and detail. Low-end is quick, but lacks impact and a bit of texture. Notes are on the lighter side, not very full, male vocals are a little thin and recessed. Not very dynamic but clean and balanced, but can be borderline clinical. NOT RECOMMENDED past 60dbs or so, gets too shrill and fatiguing in the treble with a slight metallic timbre in the treble depending on the song. Doesn't scale very well and not that immersive, but overall very technical IEM.

name: Dunu DK3001 Braindamage
notes: Technical, but thin, and bright tilt with LOTS of planar sizzle and timbre. Needs more low-end (small scoop), noteweight is very light, not peaky, but just artificial. Needs 10hm adapter to be balanced. Not a high volume set.

name: Thieaudio Oracle MK2
notes: CLEAR with LOTS of detail. Nice sub-bass rumble with no mid-bass bleed. Treble is super extended as well as high-mids. Female vocals sound lively and sings, but can be too much at high volume and overly thin. Great imaging and separation. Artificially boosted treble, too sharp.

name: Kefine Arnar
notes: Smooth, dark-leaning sound with a heavy and thumpy mid-bass. Vocals are still clear, balanced, and extended but just doesn't have the extra micro-nuances. Sounds a lot fuller and thicker than graph suggests and reminds me of a cleaner Doscinco. Scales very good and recommended for higher volumes to reach full potential since it can sound a bit congested without volume. Bass slam is very satsifying and has a more drawn out decay to simulate a heavier impact. Great for hiphop, rap, jazz, but not as technical as other sets around its price. Niche listen - an analogy would be a cup of black coffee.

name: LETSHUOER DX1
notes: Dynamic, vibrant, and contrasty vocals with good balance and scaling. Natural, full, and immersive with scaling and not peaky.

name: HIDIZS MK12 RED NOZZLE
notes: HIGH VOLUME SET 75dbs+. Insane scaling, better than DX1 scaling wise, amazing musicality, non-fatiguing, warm, but also has powerful/extended vocals. Great for male vocals, husky, but not congested or nasally. Super immersive, intimate but big sounding without feeling congested. Tip rec: TRI Clarions.

name: Simgot EM6L Phoenix Unit Variance
notes: Great resolution and tech, one of the smoothest iems, but uppermids will get hot on energetic tracks at higher volumes. Slightly warm but also lively. Recent units are brighter than first batch.

name: Simgot EA500LM
notes: Very resolving for its price, great value. A warmer EA1000 with a slight decrease in separation and resolution, but warmer with more bass (same bass quality). Not as sparkly and resolving as the EA1000s, treble is a little sharp/not as refined, but a better all-rounder. Has unit variance, lots of brighter units.

name: CCA HYDRO
notes: The best KZ so far, tuning swithces allow lots of options. Good tech, all-rounder sound with bass boost, but, KZ.

name: Hidizs MP145 OG
notes: A less sharp and sizzly HeyDay. All-rounder sound with good tech. Tamer Harman/df. Solid all-rounder.

name: MYER AUDIO CKLVX
notes: Meta-tuned all-rounder. A cheaper kiwiears astral with sharper treble.

name: 7Hz Crinacle Divine
notes: Clean, balanced, slightly dynamic, but smooth enough. Slightly lively-neutral tuning that's good for vocal/ballads. Could use more low-end and may be a bit lean for certain libraries, but overall good tech and layering.

name: Simgot Supermix 5
notes: Clean, balanced, non-fatiguing, and well-balanced with a slight bounce in the sub-bass. Smoother/less energetic version of the SM4 with better scaling, but not as technical and more expensive. BCD isn't very prominent, and price is a bit high given it sounds very close to the Divine - should be priced around $150-180. Sounds fine, but no sauce or insane value like the SM4 - wait for sale.

name: LETSHUOER S12 Ultra
notes: Smoothest S12 so far with fun sub-bass and good transients/dynamics. Slight v-shape, similar to the Defiant but a little more bassy. 1.5K vocal peak can be an issue on songs with no bass to cover it, but overall fine on most songs. Not as technical as OG S12/Pro, and not as good value vs cheaper planars, but trade of is Ultra is more refined, natural, and musical - I think the slight hit is worth it for a more enjoyable sound.

name: SIMGOT EG280
notes: All-rounder with pinpoint imaging and slight uppermids/vocal emphasis. Basically a more technical EW300 with better vocal clarity and extension. Solid for gaming like EM6L, and would be my pick since it's more natural/less bright vs EM6L.

name: LETSHUOER S12 2024
notes: The most refined S12 to date. Smoothest treble out of all the S12, and very little Planar timbre while keeping up the great tech and detail.

name: Tanchjim Ola 2 3.5MM + T500B TIPS
notes: Balanced all-rounder with firm mid-bass over sub tuning, full note-weight, natural, resolving, and good dynamics. Same driver as other Tanchjim single DD with an extra treble BA. T500 B tips makes treble sound extra airy and feels like an $100+ treble IEM. Not super different/unique but is competitive as a budget do-it-all type of IEM, scaling is mid-volume due to the transients, but with T500 B tips the treble is smooth and more refined/airy than the Defiants, and reminds me of an airier/better all-rounded Magic One.

name: Tanchjim KARA
notes: Clean and natural midrange focused signature, natural vocal extension, open and airy staging with good instrument layering. Smooth but could use more sub-bass rumble and dynamics.

name: Kiwiears Airoso
notes: A sightly more airy/detailed EW300 with better timbre. Warm leaning all rounder with good dynamic contrast.

name: Tanchjim Fola
notes: Same driver as Fission and very very similar tuning, not much of an audible difference, just has better build accessories. If you want sound just get Fission, Fola basically just a better packged Fission/Nora.

name: Tanchjim Fission
notes: Clean, non-fatiguing, balanced, full, and smooth all-rounder. Exact same driver and tuning as the Origin (with middle dial on S-SILVER NOZZLE) but with less premium build/design/cable/case - a welcomed hit for better value.

name: Tanchjim Nora
notes: Same tuning as origin and fission but without the newest driver, not much a difference sounds very similar.

name: Tanchjim Origin
notes: Just buy Fission. A cleaner/less warm LM, smoother EA1000 (fermats a little more resolving), very balanced, clean, and neutral sound. Very tough competition.

name: Kefine Quatio
notes: A bassy all-rounder, and cleaner Doscinco for $100 less. Very versatile with the different nozzles - goes from bassy to clean all-rounder. Solid packaging and accesories. Competitive tech, but not as value like Supermix4/EM6L/EA500LM.

name: TinHifi T6 Pink Nozzle
notes: Bassy all-rounder like the EW300 and Impact but with more treble emphasis/sharper imaging. Would not recommend the other nozzles as they're too bright/sharp. Seen these go as low as $90 on sale.

name: KiwiEars ETUDE
notes: Reverby, bouncy, and extended decay in the sub-bass. Unique bass play back and adds more texture to the low-end. Although reverb can bleed into the vocals - maybe the drivers work too well lol. A bassier 5+2 with better texutre and scaling.

name: Softears Volume S
notes: Relaxed, slightly warm-neutral tuning, a bit boring, full, could use more treble/air. Not as good as high volume (recommended listening vol).

name: Intuaura Impact
notes: A EW300 with better bass texture and smoother treble without the hard PZT timbre. Good bassy all-rounder. Can't find any for sale?

name: LETSHUOER S15
notes: Neutral and laid back tuning. Great layering and separation and resolution. Great treble extension and air without being too sharp and light like other planar iems. Bass is also not light and floaty, and doesn't feel like planar bass - not slamming, but tight and well-textured. Vocals are laid back, but not too pushed back although it's not the most extended and powerful, but works very-well as a neutral set. Nice and open staging, and is the direct upgrade to the Hexa and Sonus. Very good safe all-rounder.

name: AFUL PERFORMER 5+2
notes: Clean, balanced, neutral sound with good layering and tech. Relaxing vocals, but lacks power and last bit of vocal extension. Bass has good controll, but lacks impact. Has sizzly planar timbre in the treble. Safe but forgettable.

name: TinHifi P1 MAX 2
notes: Solid all-rounder for those who like a less bright Nova in the uppermids. Good for jpop/kpop. Timbre is good and not too "planar", bass texture/impact could be better.

name: Moondrop Blessing 2 Dusk
notes: Great resolution and separation. Vocals can sound recessed/thin, and is sibilant at higher volumes. Uneven and grainy treble. Clinical, thin, and not as musical as others sets.

name: MYER SLA3
notes: Dynamic all-rounder, slightly energetic with great contrast in the uppermids and bass. Solid tech, and sound is different enough from other $100 sets. Good sidegrade to safer picks like SM4, NOVA, EM6L. Uppermids can be peaky on certain songs, and not as smooth as nova/em6l/sm4, but more engaging with better dynamic contrast.

name: LETSHUOER EJ07
notes: Mid-vol ranking. Clean, mid-range focused, but treble is dark and a bit hard to hear at lower volumes. Needs to be cranked up to hear the details. Imaging, spearation, and staging is top tier, if it weren't for the lower sharpness/not as sparkly, 07 at higher volumes would be an S for tech.

name: Dunu VULKAN
notes: Neutral bass glide, full mids, and decent treble extension. Some masking and not as technical vs blessing series, but better note-weight and timbre/tonality.

name: IO Sogno
notes: Literally Harman 2019. Inoffensive and good all-rounder. A little sharp in the timbre vs Volare (I'd just save up for the Volare if you want Harman), more low-end than Volare, better bass and timbre than Supermix4 but not as good in value.

name: TinHifi T7
notes: Harman 2019

name: Moondrop Harmon
notes: Clean Harman 2019 sound. Clear and balanced, but can still be shouty in the vocals. New Crossover and 3DD talk is marketing jargon not that much difference vs other DDs. You can just buy Nova or SUPERMIX4 if you want Harman for more than half the price. Or DynnaQuattro and Chopin is better as well. Sounds "decent" but just overpriced. Also looks like a knockoff cybertruck from temu. Avoid unless you can find it for around $150 or less.

name: Tang Zu x HBB HeyDay
notes: Clean and neutral with treble emphasis. Great technical performance. Airy and lively treble. Bass could use more impact and weight. Vocals are on the lighter side of things.

name: Kinera Celest Relentless
notes: Slight v-shape with good tech and detail, treble can be too much but has that sizzle and sparkliness some people will like.

name: TangZu Wu Zetian Legend
notes: Treblehead set with lots of treble detail, great tech, but may be too spicy/overboosted for most people. Feels unnatural and fatiguing on lots of tracks unless at lower volumes. OG WU & HEYDAY are both tuned better although not as good in the tech.

name: 7Hz Aurora
notes: Mini MEST, OCD treble detail, sharp imaging, great detail and tech for its price, immersive with the right song, but is too sharp with energetic tracks with lots of electronic elements, vocals also a bit shouty, not fully extended. Bass texture si great, big DD. Good for slower genres like indie, acoustics, singer-song writer, as well as rock (hi-hats and cymbals feel very OCD/bombards you). A niche set, but does have that "special sauce".

name: Softears Volume S
rawName: Softears Volume S $319 (switch boost/ mid vol)
notes: Cleaner Harman 2019 with less sub-bass and more air. Good tech, but can be a bit clinical, and doesn't scale as well/not as musical as stock switch.

name: Dunu 242
notes: Dead neutral water. Makes Mega 7 sound like soda. If you want a monitor set with little sub-bass and dynamics this is it. Good tech, but just so bland. I'd go Tea Pro SE or even Mega 7. (Unit variance? Gonna try another set)

name: CVJ Mythera
notes: Ow. Very forward vocals but treble is not smooth enough which just makes everything sound sharp and v shaped. Tried to make a Kinera Loki but failed.

name: OG Tin Hifi P1 MAX
notes: Mid-centric, relaxing, warm, airy, comforting. Very unique listening experience. Could use better separation/resolution and bass slam.

name: AFUL Explorer
notes: High volume set, very immersive, scales great with no sharpness, wide staging, enough detail/extension, good bass, just crank it up and enjoy the music.

name: FATFREQ HBB DEUCE
notes: The defacto basshead rec before the more expensive stuff. Super fun sub-bass, textured, heavy, prolonged decay for more reverb in the bass, well-balanced as well, smooth and scales great. Tech is not its strong point, and DON'T buy from FatFreq directly!!!

name: TangZu HE Xiao Qiao
notes: All-rounder with slight vocal pop that adds extra bit of air and energy - very good for female vocals. A more vocal centric EW300 with smoother treble and better extended/sparklier vocal playback.

name: 7Hz Sonus 2
notes: Clean, balanced with good transients/dynamics, separation, and imaging - literally a better PRS6 for music. Versatile set if you don't want too much low-end but still engaging and non-fatiguing at mid-volume.

name: SIMGOT EW300 DSP with 3.5/4.4 cable
notes: Swapping the DSP cable to a 3.5/4.4mm will give you basically the same sound as stock 3.5mm EW300, so you end up getting 4 different tunings if you have a spare cable lying around. Nice.

name: SIMGOT EW300 3.5MM
notes: A smoother and more refined version of the EW200 with better layering and resolution bump. Pink nozzle is warmer and better for rock/hiphop/metal. Very good piezo implementation.

name: Juzear Nimbus Black Nozzles
notes: Natural, full, all-rounder with good extension and timbre. Good nozzle variety, well extended treble with smooth extension. Balanced but not boring and harman/jm-1 tuned. Prefer this sound wise over Lightshuttle and Defiant.

name: 7th Acoustic x QoA RYUSEI Normal Rank
rawName: 7th Acoustic x QoA RYUSEI ($129) Normal Rank
notes: Natural, extended, clear, and detailed vocals with slight shine and sparkle in the endnotes. Has the "sauce" for female vocals and excels on slower genres that allows the artist to be in focus. Feels like I'm getting hit by a ray of light like the RSV, but not as forward and full but has more glimmer and shimmer in the attack of the treble. Lots of mico-nuances from the artists' breathe and lingering notes and creates a sense of intimacy other balanced vocal sets don't offer. One of, if not the best female vocals under $350 - incredible value for vocals. The cable is also sick for $80. Only nitpick would be the bass texture could be better with more weight/slam, and that the treble can get fatiguing with kpop/jpop energetic genres (which I don't recommend listening to with these anyways). Could use more low-end or smoother treble as an all-rounder, vocals can also get thin on busier tracks that aren't vocal focused or striped back. Not as versatile as the EW300 or Defiant, but still good tech for the price, and a bright/clean sidegrade to those.

name: 7th Acoustic Stargazer
notes: A mini supernova with better sub-bass extension, but not as smooth, airy, and "technical". Probably still one of the best all-rounders around $100.

name: Juzear x Zeos Defiant GAMING
notes: All-rounder slight-v with thinner lowermids that can make feel vocals too light (artists lacking in power and extension). 95% similar to the OG Defiant with a tiny bit more treble energy - change is so small it's more like a unit variance. Basically a reskin and now comes with mic and usbc.

name: Juzear x Zeos Defiant
notes: Another all-rounder with good balance, slight v-shape, and sharp in the treble. Doesn't do anything right or wrong, but has qc issues with channel imbalance (and also my case ziper broke within a few weeks), it's ok but there are better value out there.

name: Heartfield CU8
notes: Warmer Harman 2019 with less shouty vocals. Bassy all-rounder with decent tech. Build and plate design is very pretty... but price is a bit high and not that competitive - wait for sale unless you really dig the look.

name: EarAcoustic Genesis
notes: Bassy/warm all-rounder with lots of low-end slam/body while vocals are still extended. Good for male vocals, "smooth, bassy, musical" but low-end texture can feel a bit boomy and not as well controlled/tactile as Impact and T6 (and also 2x more). Overall transients and detail not that resolving for the price, maybe if you want something warm - try to get these on sale for around $120.

name: ZIIGAAT CINNO on sale
notes: Good intrument separation/layering, but feels like the music is cut into certain areas in the stage and not harmonious (UPDATE: tip rolling helped, the fit was a little weird like the OG Dark Magician). Resolution is good, but isn't that clear and can be a little bit dark at mid-lower volumes, but the FR highlights guitars/insturments very well. Sub-bass is also good, but mid-bass feels light like the Hexa. Another neutral set like the Hexa but with better sub-bass, less gain, better scaling, although at the cost of darker treble.

name: Tanchjim Oxygen 02
notes: Amazing tuning and tech. A more resolving Hana. Great imaging but not as 3D as Tea. Fit may be a little shallow.

name: HISENIOR MEGA5P ULTRA
notes: A mini EJ07M with more forward vocals and less technical, good all-rounder, vocals can be a bit much at higher volume

name: AFUL Performer 5
notes: Fun slight v-shape tuning with forward vocals with slight excitement in the treble. Separation takes a hit as a result, and treble is a bit uneven.

name: Truthear PURE
notes: Warm/dark, laid-back, smooth, scales great like the Explorer but more vocal centric (great for male vocals). Immersive with scaling, but not the best value - Less technical than HEXA & Cinno. A warmer Cinno basically, and a warmer mini Volume S.

name: LETSHUOER DZ4
notes: $40 on sale, clean, smooth. vocal/mid-range focused. Recommended at high volumes. A better Galileo with more treble/air. Vocal centric. Powerful and extended vocals. Could use better separation and tech, and lacks bass.

name: Tanchjim 4U
notes: Solid IEM. Warm to neutral depending on the switch. Overall pretty smooth with good tech.

name: ARTTI T10 PRO
notes: A mini symphonium Meteor. Bassy, warm, and airy/smooth.

name: NICEHCK NX8
notes: An Explorer with better vocals but doesn't scale as well. Odyssey and Arcadia better for clean and bass sound.

name: AFUL Magic One on sale
notes: Balanced and neutral with slight warmth in the mid-bass. Male vocals are great on these, weighted but still has edge and sharpness to the end notes, but can get sharp at higher volumes. Male vocals are bit congested, not the most open need the right tips (CLARION). Stage is average, and treble is smooth with solid extension for the most part, tech is around Hexa/EM6L level which is great for a single BA. Great neutral-warm/all-rounder overall, it's pretty much an adjusted diffuse-field with more mid-bass. I personally don't get the hype/"magic" behind these.

name: Kefine Klean SV Black Nozzles
notes: Balanced and clean all-rounder in the black nozzles with options of being a vocal set with silver and gold nozzles. A cleaner and more technical version of the OG Klean while maintaining dynamics. Can potentially get lean/sharp due to lower bass shelf.

name: Apple AirPods Pro 2
notes: Great sense of depth with improvement in soundstage over OG. More precise imaging, and improvement in seperation and overall clarity. Treble is better exteded. Sub-bass is around the same with more mid-bass. Vocals are more pushed back vs OG. Overall welcomed improvements.

name: Tripowin HBB Olina SE
notes: Bright all-rounder. Cheapest holographic staging you can get. Very smooth overall with little uneveness. Double Olina filter mod (or SE version) fixes the uppermid and treble brightness from OG while maintaining technicalities. Smoother and better fit than Airship. Get it on sale.

name: Kefine Delci AE Silver Nozzle
notes: A smoother EW200 with the silver nozzles (although vocals are better on the EW200). Bronze nozzle can be too bright and peaky, but brings up the technacilities

name: 7Hz Elua Ultra
notes: A mini Astral, meta slight v tuning, fun, dynamic while being smooth enough, good tech for price, solid rec

name: Tanchjim Bunny Gaming DSP/3.5MM Cable
notes: New upgraded driver based on the DMT5 (modified) and better than the DMT4 Ultra. Sound wise very similar to OG Bunny but now with a slight detail/resolution boost. Still has the versatility with the DSP APP with recommend EQ being "Pop", or swap DSP cable with 3.5mm cable to change the sound to a more mid-bass leaning bass shelf which I prefer more (but you can also just custom EQ this in the APP). Overall great value tech and versatility wise while still sounding engaging/dynamic and not too peaky. Default DSP, balanced, and nature EQ is not really recommended due to the lean bass, thinness, and shouty uppermids. Go Pop EQ for all-rounder sound, or Ambient. 3.5MM stock sounds best tho.

name: Tangzu HBB Xuan NV
notes: A smoother hexa, and mini-nova. Very clean and balanced all-rounder. Good vocal set. Harman 2019 with more mid-bass, less uppermids and sub-bass. Nothing crazy, but does every genre very well.

name: Moondrop Aria 2 RED
notes: A slightly more vocal centric Aria 2, slightly less soft in the overall texture due to less air. Balanced-clean all-rounder. A bit pricy at $100, wait for sale.

name: Moondrop Kadenz
notes: Literally a more fancy Tangzu Xuan NV. Sounds basically the same but just with better packaging, cable/case, and build... but for $100 more?? Nah

name: BQEYZ Winter
notes: Clean and open signature with slight treble emphasis. Not airy, but more sharp. Great resolution and imaging. Relatively safe tuning.

name: Punch Audio Portazo
notes: Basshead set, a more v shaped 7Hz Diablo. Punchy, full, meaty, deep rumbly bass with a heavy slam. Vocals can be a bit recessed on busier tracks as well as hit in layering. A mini Martilo/HBB Punch without the tech and balance but better scaling/warmer/smoother.

name: 7Hz Crinacle Diablo
notes: Bassy, dynamic, non-fatiguing, good scaling. Great bass slam, texture, with tight control. Fun lowkey basshead set. Might be too warm and congested for vocals/instrumentals. Priced $50 higher than I'd like.

name: Symphonium Giant
notes: Super warm and thick, mid-bass centric, basically the Meteor with less treble and more low-end, needs power, turns into basshead at higher volumes, very bassy.

name: SIMGOT EW300 DSP
notes: A mini Dynaquattro, clean, balanced, vocal focused versus the 3.5mm version. Scales very good and smoothly with pink nozzles. Slight hit in imaging and transients vs 3.5mm version.

name: ORIVERTI OD200
notes: A warmer EA1000 with less treble energy. Treble quality is great, smooth, refined with Silver nozzle. Black nozzle too spicy.

name: Dunu PRS6
notes: Neutral flat with no bass and very little treble extension. Why use MEMS if you're going to kill the treble anyways?? Somehow still peaky and brittle at higher volumes? Only good thing about it is the clean midrange and competitive layering, but sounds too soft in the transients at mid/lower volumes to make any worthwhile differences in gaming. Literally a worse version of the Crinear Reference since that's the more detailed & natural flat IEM. Also a worse version of the P5+2 treble wise and overall bass dynamics. Also a worse version of the Silicons. Sharp wing edge stabs into my ears and can't wear for more than an hour. Somehow made a fatiguing IEM that you can't scale, AND a gimped treble/bass IEM that also sounds soft/smoothed out at lower volumes.

name: Kiwi Ears Melody
notes: Fun signature done right. Sparkly and energetic V-SHAPE, but with punchy bass and not bloated for under $100 - how? Can get a bit sharp with certain tracks.

name: Crinear Nightfall
notes: Smooth, inoffensive, balanced, JM-1 bass boost. Put it on and forget about it type of set. Will not wow you but will not hurt you either. Detail/texture is not that good for the price. Uppermids cut also hurts vocal detail and clarity. Bass texture, impact, rumble is passable but will not "get you going". Get it on sale if you want something safe that you can use in the background.

name: EPZ x Tipsy STAR ONE
notes: Vocal focused set. Female vocals are sweet and clean with subtly air and sparkle. Treble and bass is decent, does the job. Harman but with a twist.

name: Shozy P20 on sale
notes: Unique tuning with "speical sauce", warm but also sparkly in the treble without the uppermids becoming shouty (tamer uppermids). Great for kpop/jpop/pop and even hiphop and rock. Gives you that splashy ocd feeling in the treble but also still warm. Timbre is decent, not as offensive as the other planars. Vocal details/texture does take a step back as a trade off for less shout.

name: LETSHUOER S08
notes: More uniquely tuned than other planars. Tamer uppermids, not as energetic, but still with great bass separation and tech. Timbre is good.

name: Softear Studio 2
