notes: HIGH VOLUME SET (at least 75dbs+). Warm, comfy, vintage-like sound with great immersion. Vocals are somehow still clear at higher volume and not overly dark. Not very good tech to $$ value wise, but very unique sounding. Would not recommend for mid to lower volume listening as it'll sound too dark, congested, and "low-res". Needs scaling.

name: BEYERDYNAMICS DT30 IE
notes: Flat, neutral, dark, high-scaling set made for musicians on stage. A bit too flat to be enjoyable for audiophile listening, but if you need an affordable non-fatiguing uncolored sound for performances, these are decent and don't break the bank.

name: Apevoix Grit
notes: A better tuned Anvil, but BCD doesn't do much, bassy all-rounder sound

name: Penon DOME
notes: Warm, intimate sound without being too bassy and bloated. Vocals are forward and very immersive. Resolution not that competitive, but a very musical set.

name: FATfreq Maestro Mini
notes: A basshead set that's actually well-balanced for the most part. Extension on uppermids/highs are good but can get shouty, sub-bass texture and slam is impactful and satisfying - this is the set for most bassheads who don't want a crap ton of bass but still a good amount. Deuce better.

name: INTUARA SPLENDOR VIEW 2
notes: Slight v-shape that's well done. Well-rounded, nothing much wrong with it. Good all-rounder.

name: QoA Bijou
notes: Mid-bass centric all-rounder with good extension in the vocals and overall dynamics. Low-end is engaging with nice slam, weight, and impact without hurting vocal timbre and extension. Sudden rise around 2-3k can get shouty and peaky on certain tracks, and treble is also on the peakier side without too much air, making the sound less open due to the added mid-bass. Okay for $80 if you want a mid-bass all-rounder, and can handle the 2-3K gain.

name: Juzear 61t
notes: Low-end is good, tight, with good impact, but bass feels low-res. Vocals are too recessed and warm. Treble and air is good, but that's about it. BA timbre. Relaxing listen, but Dynaquattro is just the better version of it imo, better bass texture, clarity, vocals. Too much competition around it.

name: FATfreq Scarlet Mini
notes: Crap ton of sub-bass but still very well-controlled (for the most part). No mud or mid-bass bloat, uppermids/treble are smoother than Maestro Mini, still somewhat balanced without having the low-end overtake. Vocals do distort sometimes as the sub-bass can bleed into it. Deuce better.

name: FlipEars AEGIS
notes: Slight v-shape, but with less bass and low-end texture than Legion, more "balanced" and less engaging, but my unit was shouty and a bit sharp in the uppermids, also costs alot for what you can get at under $100.

name: Kiwi Ears CANTA
notes: Bright set with lots of treble detail. Airy, splashy, and shimmery with great extension. Isn't sharp or metallic in the timbre, but not 100% "natural" either, comes down to preference. Mid-volume set, good with slower genres, not rec for high energy tracks, can get much at higher volumes. Favors female vocals, male could be a bit light and could use more power, but vocals aren't thin or shrill sounding like the Oracle MK2s. Not gonna float everyone's boat, but it's a unique listen (not the same planar tuning yay) and worth having as a collectors piece.

name: LETSHUOER S12 PRO
notes: A less bright timeless/S12.

name: NICEHCK F1 PRO
notes: A cheaper S12. Almost identical sound and tuning. Good value. Look for aliexpress deals.

name: Kefine Klanar
notes: A cheaper S12. Almost identical sound and tuning. Good value. Look for aliexpress deals.

name: LETSHUOER S12
notes: A timeless with spicier treble.

name: 7Hz Timeless Outdated unless sale
notes: Great details. Good stage in front but lacking in wideness/3D. Imaging is good and speration is great, but uneven treble peaks. Planar timbre. Vocals and notes can be thin. Fatiguing at higher volume listening.

name: Simgot EA2000
notes: Very clean with great resolution, but vocals can be too bright (alot of gain). Bass-texture is great with decent treble extension. Amazing for female vocals, but again, can get shouty. A brighter EA1000.

name: ARTTI T10 lowest
notes: A cheaper S12. Almost identical sound and tuning. INSANE value. Look for aliexpress deals.

name: TINHIFI DUDU
notes: Least planar, almost doesn't sound like one. 3K gain can be a bit much, tech very similar as the other ones.

name: Truthears HEXA
notes: Foam helps tame uppermids/treble. Great detail for price and new benchmark below $100. Better tuned "softer" Dusk with slighlty less accurate imaging. Note-weight can be light. Still decent on sale in 2025 if you want something neutral/clean.

name: Moondrop Starfield 3
notes: Neutral/bright leaning with flat mids, vocals sound a bit stuffed/wonky in the timbre and a bit hidden on busier songs. Decent detail retreival and layering, imaging is good, but sub-bass is non-existent - just get Kaiser.

name: SIVGA Nightingale
notes: If you get a boosted treble unit then it'd be ranked here...VERY GENRE SPECIFIC. Listen at high volume with slower tracks (slow rock, ballads, indie, jazz, blues, acoustics, instrumentals etc). TOTL stage, layering, treble detail, but vocals and sub-bass are rolled-off/pushed back, losing details there otherwise would be at least be S- for tech. Treble can also be too energetic depending on the unit (a lot of them graph with lots of treble - mine doesn't sound that boosted), so in-general NOT RECOMMENDED for libraries with a lot of sub-bass (rolled-off) or energy (too sharp if you get a boosted unit). That aside, gives me OG EJ07 vibes immersion wise. Hard to recommend because unit variations.

name: LETSHUOER x AOSHIDA E20 EQ
notes: BASS EQ VERSION. 2DD setup like Deuce but with a 10mm Berylium DD. Slight step-up in resolution, staging, and detail over the Deuce. Deuce bass still goes deeper, harder, and fuller with more reverb (better as basshead). EQ: (Peak 20hz, +2.5db, Q:2), (Peak 35hz, +7db, Q:0.5), (Peak 40hz, -1db, Q:1.3), (Peak 120hz, +1.5db, Q:1), (Low-shelf 150hz, +1.5db, Q:1), (Peak 320hz, -1db, Q:2), (Peak 1500hz, -1.5db, Q:1).

name: SIVGA SM100 300 Mesh Mod + TRI Clarion Tips inTotal
rawName: SIVGA SM100 300 Mesh Mod + TRI Clarion Tips  $60 inTotal
notes: Vocal/mid-range focused with great timbre and noteweight. Smooth treble for the price with great extension. Very great vocal all-rounder under $100.

name: Truthear Crinacle Blue 2 5ohm adapter
notes: Mini HBB Punch. Fun basshead sound with impedance adapter. Extra bass helps balance out the uppermids/treble making it more enjoyable than stock.

name: Tanchjim Hana 2021
notes: An Oxygen with more bass and note-weight but at the cost of slightly worse imaging and detail.

name: EPZ Q5 PRO
notes: Fun slight v while being balanced, good resolution, engaging sound

name: TangZu Yu Xuan Ji
notes: Airy treble/staging. Clean balanced sound. Good tech. 8-10K Peak isn't as big as graph suggests.

name: Kinera Celest IgniteX Beast
notes: All-rounder with good tech and imaging. Dynamic and engaging bass and treble. A less in your face EW200.

name: KZ Duonic
notes: Replaces the CCA Trio (discontiued in many places), very similar sound but less v shape, less uppermids and sub-bass (well, at least my unit). Great value for the price, but your unit may vary cuz KZ.

name: CCA TRIO
notes: Well-balanced to endgame ie with bassy option as well, good tech for the price, soild all-rounder beginner set, $20 on sale, but kz

name: Simgot EW200
notes: Bright leaning all-rounder harman adjusted sound. Very technical and detailed for price but can get too eenrgetic/bright depending on the unit.

name: SIVGA Que
notes: Warm and engaging set with good energy and extension when it comes to vocals, could use more air, but overall very fun and bassy set

name: CCA PHOENIX
notes: Balanced, clean, vocal centric set, great detail and layering for price, imaging is sharp, but bass can be light and not as engaging, and uppermids/treble can be shouty.

name: EPZ Q1 PRO
notes: Literally OG 7hz Zero with a better driver, better clarity and resolution. Clean balanced sound. Vocal/mid focused. Treble can get peaky at times. Overall solid value tech wise but a little lean in the low-end.

name: TRI Starsea
notes: Deep bass and good treble. Mids/vocals can sound reccessed. Good imaging and separation. No real complaints.

name: Tripowin HBB Kailua on sale
notes: Great all-rounder. A more exciting Olina SE with bump in sharpness and bass texture (Olina SE still more 3D). Driver feels fast and detailed. Sweet female vocals and treble extension. Nice bass slam. DD timbre. No real complaints - open stage although hurt by masking which can feel like there's "holes"; masking also affects female vocals (not completely extended), but very resolving for its price, although can use better separation.

name: DUNU Titan S2
notes: Very nice built and cable for the price. Sounds like a warm harman. Tech is good, but not too competitive at the price (EA500LM).

name: Simgot EA500 OG
notes: Slamming bass with the variety. High quality DD with good resolution.

name: Dunu Kima 2
notes: Warm-neutral, relaxing set, great cable, build, and accessories. Vocals are a bit soft, not fully extended, could use more air, but overall decent if you want a comfortable listen

name: Etymotic ER2XR
notes: An ER2SE with better bass control.

name: Moondrop Kato
notes: Good detail, clarity, and imaging, but can sound thin. Similar tuning as Hana, but I found Hana to have better note-weight and bass.

name: HBB KZ PR2 OG
notes: New batch needs 300-500 mesh filters

name: HISENIOR T4
notes: Aria 2 with more tuning options (warmer) and slight bump in tech

name: PULA Anvil
notes: Good low-end impact and slam, but boomy/soft in the bass texture, the BCD has no effect in the low-end, more prominent in the uppermids/treble which can lead to some sharp/graininess/jaggity timbre. Feels like they tried to copy the Tea Pros but failed, worse in both tuning and driver quality - I'd just get the D62 or save up for the Tea Pros

name: Truthears HEXA
notes: Amazing detail for price and new benchmark below $100. Better tuned "softer" Dusk with slighlty less accurate imaging. Note-weight can be light.

name: CCA RHAPSODY
notes: Sub-bass focused slight v-shape, fun and engaging with lots of bass switch options, treble is smooth for the price, vocals are nicely extended... but there is a scoop in the lower-midrange that affects vocals and has a hollow thin timbre to the sound - which also makes vocals a bit shouty and shrill at higher volumes. It also sounds very similar to the Castor Bass edition which is 3x cheaper - although it has better layering and treble, if you're looking for bass I'd just save my money and grab the castor/pro bass.

name: Truthear Crinacle Blue 2 Stock
notes: Fun sub-woofer sound in the low-end, nice bouncy textue, but uppermids/treble can be too bright, especially with 15K treble peak. Basically a more v-shaped version of the OG TE Zeros. Vocals can be a bit shouty and thin.

name: Truthears Crinacle Zero
notes: Variations-ish tuning with sub-bass focused. Low-end is rumbly but lacks mid-bass impact/warmness in general. Fatiguing above mid-volume. Can sound light and thin. Mid-bass tuck affects libraries.

name: ALPHA & DELTA KS100 TWS
notes: BEST subwoofer bass I've heard for a TWS under $100. What the Singolo should've been. If you want sub-bass, these are it. Very good for the gym. Uppermids can be bright, suggested EQ: Peak Filter, 4000khz, -3.5dbs, Q1

name: Kinera Celest Mimosa
notes: Slight v-shape, vocals a bit recesed at mid-volume, treble PZT timbre, vocals sounds wonky

name: BQEYZ WIND
notes: Bright-neutral with sharp transients. If you like treble you'll like this. Bass texture is solid, reminds me of the EA1000s. Not that smooth, slightly energetic/lively sound.

name: EPZ K5
notes: Clean, uppermids focused with slight scope at 500hz that can make it sound clinical and sharp in female vocals, however, great resolution and great for acoustic instrumentals.

name: EPZ 620
notes: Genre dependent. Mini U12T with all the hollow/pushed back vocals and sharpness at high volumes, BUT, grand staging, great layering, and sharp imaging that works incredibly well with instrumentals/non-vocal tracks

name: ORIVETI Dynabird
notes: Vocal focused and clean, but 2K gain can be too much plus the uppermids/treble. Good tech.

name: Samsung Galaxy Buds2 Pro
notes: Very well tuned with slight v-shape. Bass is detailed with good texture and treble has good extension. Soundstage is average and lacks width; less open and expansive than AirPods Pro 2s. Imaging and separation is also good but slightly behind the AP2. Vocals and treble are more forward with more bite vs AP2. More exciting vs the AP2 that's more balanced and laid back. Detail and clarity are similar vs AP2, but treble and bass is more emphasized and takes more of one's focus.

name: Etymotic ER2SE
notes: Great detail & clarity. Fit took a long time to get used. Very clear and natural mids and treble. Lacks lower-extension, and couldn't handle bass notes on Time by Hikaru Utada (0:40+).

name: SeeAudio X Crinacle Midnight
notes: Great vocals and mids. Sub-bass boost and smooth treble. Overall great tuning but lacking in upper frequency details and imaging/seperation. Average soundstage.

name: Tripowin x Olina OG
notes: Bright Oxygen with deeper fit+more treble air results in better soundstage. Great for mid volume, but fatiguing vocals and treble at higher volume. Mod needed for higher volume/longer listening.

name: LETSHUOER x AOSHIDA E20
notes: Stock non-EQ. Clean, balanced tuning with nice bass texture. Could use more body in the low-end and fill in the mid-bass scoop, or less uppermids. Good tech

name: 7Hz FIVE
notes: V-shaped, a lot of bass, good slam and impact. Fun and exciting. Texture is ok, layering and separation not that clean. Uppermids are sharp. Vocals are husky/congested and sharp somehow. Lack of air stage is small. Doesn't scale well, can't listen past 65dbs ish.

name: SIVGA QUE UTG
notes: High energy, sharp transients, bright/v-shape, aggresive treble, lean low-end, good technicalities but overall timbre and dynamics are unnatural and too sharp/energetic

name: Moondrop Starfield 2
notes: Bright harman/DF, great detail, but a bit sharp and shrill

name: Tanchjim Bunny DSP/3.5MM
notes: Clean neutral (DSP) sound to slightly warm (3.5MM), very smooth for the price with great tech. Lots of tuning variety with DSP settings.

name: Tanchjim Zero ULTIMA DSP/3.5MM
notes: Clean neutral (DSP) sound to slightly warm (3.5MM), very smooth for the price with great tech. Treble not as smooth as Bunny but similar tech and better value. Lots of tuning variety with DSP settings.

name: LETSHUOER Galileo
notes: Clean and neutral signature with empahsis in the midrange. Best vocals before Orch Lite $100-->Replaced by DZ4.

name: Rosetechnics Star City 5 Pro
notes: Unique vocal focused set. Neutral low-end, tame treble. Hybrid 1DD+2BA. Some BA timbre, but vocals pop very nicely. Tech is ok.

name: Moondrop Aria 2
notes: A more engaging Aria SE with more bass, air, and reverb. Feels too smoothed out with a hit in the texture. Bump in tech over the old one, but pricing is an issue vs EW200 and EW300

name: Kefine Klean on sale
notes: Same as Delci, graph and sounds the same, but cheaper with extra tuning filter

name: HiBy YULA
notes: Slight v, full mid-bass, dynamic all-rounder, can be peaky in the vocals and uppermids, not as smooth and refined in the treble vs Klean and Zenith. I'd just grab Elua Ultra, smoother, more detailed, and also dynamic. Cable is nice tho, so maybe on sale around $20-25.

name: Kefine Delci
notes: A warmer/less sharp EW200, a slightly more resolving BLON Z300, price might be an issue tho

name: 7hertz Sonus -50 lowest
notes: A Hexa with more air/forward vocals but at the cost of layering. Resolution is similar, a little less detailed. Solid neutral/balanced set.

name: EPZ Q5
notes: Can be a bit bright on pop/edm, but very good for jazz/blues/soul and warm instrumentals.

name: Truthear PURE
notes: This is the mid/lower-volume ranking. Warm/dark, laid-back, smooth, scales great like the Explorer but more vocal centric (great for male vocals). Immersive with scaling, but not the best value - Less technical than HEXA & Cinno. A warmer Cinno basically, and a warmer mini Volume S. Not rec at mid-lower volumes.

name: Kefine Loric
notes: Bassy all-rounder, and one of the best iteration of the "mini-EW300s" budget clones so far. More clarity and treble detail than Rumba and Vivace for around the same price if not cheaper. Good bass texture and extension elsewhere while still being a more low-end focused set.

name: ORIVETI OD100
notes: A well-done slight v-shape with good technicalities. A fun starter set. Treble surprisingly smooth for the tuning and price.

name: InAwaken Mistwood
notes: All-rounder with tamer high-end and slight low-end emphasis, good for male vocals. Very nice design, packaging, and variety, but technical performance is not that competitive - more like a $30-40 IEM detail wise. Not bad overall, but I'd wait for it on sale.

name: InAwaken DAWN-Ms
notes: An OG Delci with more sub-bass rumble, and vocals pop a little more. Nice warm bassy set.

name: ARTTI R2
notes: Clean, balanced sound for the most part, slightly warm but no bleed or bloat. Very smooth. A budget Tanchjim Origin, and better Galileo sound wise IMO (more air)

name: ZIIGAAT RUMBA
notes: Natural all-rounder with good bass texture and slam, essentially a more vocal centric version of the Vivace (and mini EW300)

name: Tripowin x 0diBi Vivace
notes: A mini EW300 and a KLEAN with less treble air and detail. Rec if you can get it for $20, but otherwise save up for the KLEAN or EW300.

name: KZ Gale
notes: Clean, balanced, non-fatiguing, Harman without the uppermids boost and sub-bass. Priced well if you want a clean/more neutral leaning set that is still full enough in the mid-bass.

name: Kiwiears x B_Media Chorus
notes: Warm all-rounder with good vocals. 99% identical to Belle with the addition of open back vent that makes it a tiny tiny bit more airy. Basically a reskin. Slightly smaller in fit and slightly less occlusion effect vs Belle, but essentially the same IEM.

name: Kiwiears Belle
notes: Warm, bassy, smooth, great for scaling, only downside is tech is not the best for the price, but very "musical".

name: 7Hz HBB ELUA
notes: A fun bassy v-shape. Mini HBB Punch. Can get peaky and sharp in the treble. Use deep fitting tips.

name: BQEYZ BQ10
notes: Bassy warm set with good dynamics. Unique set some people will love. Good mid-bass texture with just enough vocals and treble.

name: ARTTI R1
notes: Bassy, warm set, good dynamics, smooth.

name: Moondrop MAY DSP
notes: Warm, intimate, but airy sound. Great accessories for the price. Warmer, and a little less resolving than EW200 and Aria 2, but DSP DAC+APP gives good versatility if no access to EQ.

name: Moondrop Rays DSP
notes: A more neutral version of the May with less bass and treble, very neutral sounding, inoffensive and boring, overpriced, many cheaper options with similar tuning and performance

name: Truthears Crinacle RED
notes: Great all-rounder, IEF-harman. Bass is a bit pillowy.

name: Moondrop Position
notes: Sounds and graphs like Chu 2 but a little cleaner/less bassy with DSP and fancier case now

name: TINHIFI T4 OG
notes: A harman/df or waner with a better driver.

name: TINHIFI T4 Plus
notes: A bright harman/df, and brigther T4.

name: TINHIFI T5
notes: A bright v-shaped harman/df, and a T4 Plus with more uppermids focus.

name: 7hertz Legato
notes: SUPER SLAMMING BASS but also well controlled and fairly open stage.

name: Kiwi Ears Quartet
notes: Lot's of variety with slamming bass.

name: KZ Vader Pro
notes: Clean vocal focused with a slight mid-bass scoop - uppermids can get shouty and not as smooth/bass texture not as good as Duonic - just get the Duonic it's a better version of this.

name: TangZu Xue Tao
notes: Bassy, warm, smooth, non-fatiguing. Not very technical and not ideal for gaming due to too much low-end hurting separation and spacial cues. A less technical version of the Klean. Kiwiears Belle similar but better value.

name: TangZu FUDU
notes: Fun/bassy harman without sacrificing much tech. Engaging low-end, and tips are also nice addition. BA timbre.

name: TINHIFI T5S
notes: A good bassy set. Great low-end texture and slam. Forward bass presentation (bass in your face). Heavier than Legato but not as well-controlled and open.

name: FiiO JD7
notes: A cheaper T5S with less sub-bass

name: TINHIFI C5
notes: A harman/df or waner with a better driver, and more vocal emphasis.

name: Moondrop Lan 2 Pop/Ref
notes: Bassy all-rounder in the pop version, and neutral/clean with sub-bass roll-off in the ref version. If these 2 were combined with tuning switch would be worth it, but curent price doesn't jusitfy the sound due to competition (klean, elua ultra, waner 2, bunny dsp etc.)

name: 7Hz G1
notes: V-shape sound, fun bass with good extension elsewhere

name: Moondrop Starfield
notes: Good soundstage/imaging, and note-weight. Aged well, although you can get the same with cheaper sets now.

name: Moondrop Aria SE
rawName: Moondrop Aria SE ($80) outdated dont buy
notes: A cleaner OG Aria with the same driver as Starfield, another harman

name: Moondrop Aria
notes: A more warmer Starfields with good thumpy bass, but bleeds into the mids. Recessed vocals. Treble peak.

name: Apple Airpods Pro
rawName: Apple Airpods Pro (TWS) ($250) outdated dont buy
notes: Neutral/safe sound with decent tech. Soundstage/imaging improves with more power/most phone amp won't pull out full potential-->Tested with iPad Pro/Mac vs iPhone.

name: Sennheiser IE200
notes: Great dynamics and scaling. Very good treble timbre and extension... but $150?? Low-end is soft, boring, and pushed back. Mid-range and vocals are recessed. Same level of clarity and tech as cheaper sets like DSP and Khan. Gets outdoned by the Hexa, Olina, Dioko for $50-70 cheaper. Horrible pricing. NEEDS EQ or MOD.

name: Kiwiears Cadenza 2
notes: A more technical and cleaner version of the OG Cadenza. Improved imaging, detail, and layering at the cost of sharper treble and not being as "musical" and engaging.

name: Heartfield Elephant
notes: V-shape, dynamic, bassy, exciting... would've been ok 3 years ago. Gets peaky and shouty and not very smooth, and also very pricey - should be under $50.

name: QoA Adonis New
notes: Warm bassy sound, needs scaling, needs more air and vocals, thick comforty sound but sounds dark and congested, treble sounds peaky and metallic

name: LETSHUOER DZ4
notes: A Galileo with more treble/air. Vocal centric. Could use better separaiton (struggles with busier tracks), and lacks bass. Needs JUICE and volume to reach full potential-->See high-volume ranking.

name: Kiwi Ears x Crinacle Singolo
notes: Why. If you like Crin just buy the RED, OG Zero, or Khan. Hype and marketing bait. Not actually "revolutionary". Avoid unless you can get these for under $40.

name: Dunu Titan X
notes: Warm leaning vocal tonality but has gapping hole around 4-8K that makes vocals feel incomplete, hollow, and unnatural. Tech is also meh for the price as it's essentially a worse version of Kiwiears Belle/Chorus, Tangzu Waner 2 Bass, and CCA Polaris.

name: Tangzu x Azla Noirblanc
notes: Shoutier Harman 2019 with even more uppermids focus. Gets peaky and fatiguing on most songs due to the boost and lean low-end. Treble air is also masked and not well-extended. Niche vocal set for ballads I guess? But aside from that a pass for most people - unfortunate because the design and accesories are nice.

name: Kiwi Ears FORTEZA
notes: Great resolution and imaging/seperation for its price. Highlights female vocals very nicely, but Uppermids gets a bit sharp + scooped lowermids. Great value tech wise, but tonality might be bright for many.

name: Tanchjim ONE 3.5MM
notes: Warm/airy all-rounder. Nice mid-bass and air for rock. Very smooth for price.

name: Kiwi Ears Cadenza
notes: Basically the modded Zero with slight more bass. Best note-weight out of the $20 sets. Berrylium bass baby.

name: Tanchjim Tanya DSP
notes: A more exciting Quarks DSP with more bass. Diffuse-field done right, great all-rounder, very smooth for price.

name: EPZ G10 on sale
notes: Clean budget Harman, highlights vocals very nicely.

name: KZ EDC PRO on sale
notes: Nicely tuned v shape, smooth treble for the price/single DD, also very cheap on sale... but KZ.

name: KBear Rosefinch
notes: Best budget basshead set. Crap ton of bass. Slams like a truck. Amazing bass weight and impact.

name: Moondrop Lan
notes: Another one

name: Moondrop Quarks DSP
notes: Super clean with great clarity. A better tuned Variations without the tech. Pinnacle of harman tuning. Although mid-bass scoop can affect some libraries.

name: SONY MH755/750 MMCX
notes: V-shape exciting tuning but with great vocal and treble clarity. Bass is clean but also slams very nice especially in the sub-bass. Mids are bit recessed and vocals gets sharp at higher volumes. Some metallic treble timbre.

name: Simgot EW100P
notes: Clean and neutral. Another Harman/df. Nothing wrong with it. Great starter set.

name: TangZu Waner 2 Nice accessories
notes: Balanced All-rounder. Basically the same as OG Waner but with a little more treble air, helps boost resolution and imaging by a tiny tiny bit. Accesories are great for the price, sancai tips + nice cable

name: Moondrop CHU 2
notes: Another harman-ish tuning. Similar to Tanchjim One but not as smooth.

name: Tangzu Wan'er
notes: Basically the modded Zero with slight more bass. Most vocal forward out of the $20 sets.

name: Truthear Gate
notes: All rounder with less uppermids than the EW100P, very close to waner.

name: ZIIGAAT NUO on sale
notes: Woohoo another harman/df! Very similar to the G10, but cheaper with heftier note-weight. Clean budget Harman, highlights vocals very nicely. Can be sharp.

name: Truthear Hola
notes: Basically the modded Zero with slight more bass, airy and least shouty $20 sets.

name: OG CCA CRA
notes: Tanya filters fixes uppermids and adds more low-end. Scales better and notes sound more weighted and fuller.

name: Tanchjim Ola
notes: Heavily library dependent. Amazing clarity, but lacks low-end. Smooth uppermids/treble with decent extension. Brighter Mini-DM.

name: Tanchjim Ola Bass
notes: A Quarks DSP without the mid-bass scoop and more air. Smooth dynamics. More "V" vs OG Ola and exciting. A less technical Olina SE.

name: Tripowin Piccolo Out of stock at
rawName: Tripowin Piccolo ($10)  Out of stock at $10
notes: Permanently on sale for $10, a steal at that price given the build and tuning is decent as well. Had some fit issues at first, but ya, another all-rounder.

name: TINHIFI T3+
notes: Another one

name: TINHIFI C3
notes: Another one

name: TangZu Wan'er S.G
notes: A cleaner version of waner with more vocal emphasis.

name: QKZ x HBB KHAN
notes: Same as the Crin Zero but with slightl more bass and less faitguing, although at the cost of more recessed vocals/mids. Mid-bass tuck affects libraries.

name: HBB Blon Z300
notes: Nicely done warm tuning. Slight upgrade to QKZ HBB.

name: Simgot EW100 DSP
notes: Basically the EW100 but with more bass and DSP timbre (lighter).

name: QKZ HBB
notes: Very well tuned warm/bassy set. Not basshead like the Rosefinch, but still has good bass impact as well as upholding enough treble extension.

name: 7hz CRIN ZERO 2
notes: Woohoo another harman/df! More bass than OG Zero, but doesn't feel as clean and open. Clarity is similar as OG Zero because of the boosted bass and decreaed treble. Z300 is a better version of this with more treble and better build/cable/packaging.

name: ND PLANET
notes: Slight vshape all-rounder with punchy bass. KZ EDC PRO better treble extension/smoother, and cheaper.

name: TangZu Chang Le
notes: The closest v-shape to the OG MH755/750

name: Kinera Celest Abyss Wyvern
notes: Sounds like a warmer harman. Very beautiful plating for its price.

name: 7hz Salnotes Zero
notes: A stock Chu with a little more bass, and smoother uppdermids/treble.

name: 7hz Aero
notes: A more v-shaped zero2 with more bass. Feels cheap.

name: Kiwi Ears Dolce (
notes: Well done V-shape. Very similar to CRA CCA+.

name: CCA Polaris
notes: Overall clean and balanced sound, but pinna gain is too much at higher volumes making vocals sound shrill and thin. Mid volume is nice, but KZ, so.

name: Moondrop JIU
notes: Another one

name: Moondrop Droplet
notes: Another one

name: Moondrop Chu 3
notes: Mid-bass focused all-rounder that has fuller/more textued low-end than Chu 2 and less shouty, but at the cost of worse clarity, treble, and detail. Worst version of the EW300 mini clones, I'd just save up and get Loric, or Zero 2/Waner 2 bass/QKZ HBB

name: HZSOUND - Heartmirror OG
notes: Very clean and vocal focused. Can sound bright at times. Good dynamics. Very library dependent. A less shouty Tanchjim Zero.

name: TANGZU HE CAI WEN JI
notes: Smooth, non-fatiguing, neutral/mid-leaning sound that needs scaling or else it will sound low-res and too dark/smoothed out. Good for vocal scaling and kpop due to the tamer uppermids. Basically a less technical and cheaper version of the Waner 2 without the bass and uppermids.

name: QKZ HBB HADES
notes: Slams even harder than the Rosefinch. If you want the most bass these are it. No vocals no treble, only bass. High-volume listening recommeded.

name: KZ Castor KZ
notes: Fun/slight-v shape with nice sub-woofer like bass (2/DD). It's KZ though so beware.

name: TRI X HBB KAI
notes: Made for loud-blasting. Great bass slam, note-weight and scaling, but a little too dark and not enough imaging/separation results in congestion and less "hifi". Staging lacks depth and air. Use it for long-sessions or high volume listening when you don't care about tech.

name: HBB KZ PR2 KZ
rawName: HBB KZ PR2 ($45) KZ not rec
notes: Silent retune killed it - needs modding

name: Sony WF-1000XM4
notes: Low-end focused, but lacks uppermids/treble extension. Bass bleeds into the mids. Muddy. Veiled. "low-res". Vocals are recessed and lack clarity; lacks clarity in general.

name: Tripowin x HBB Melee
rawName: Tripowin x HBB Melee ($50) not rec
notes: A better version of the 03.

name: Takstar TS-2300
notes: Traditional v-shape. Energetic, fun, exciting, obviously not going to be clean or balanced, but a fun experience.

name: TinHifi C0
notes: A 7hertz Zero but with less sub-bass and more air. Fit is horrendous and reminds me of the ER2SE but not as bad.

name: Moondrop Chu
notes: Nicely tuned. Great midrange and vocals with decent technicalities. Punches above its price point. Lacking in bass, spearation, and soundstange, but can't complain at $20.

name: Tanchjim Zero
notes: A Quarks DSP without the sub-bass and more uppermids - better clarity due to bass cut, but sounds more "boring"/lacks bass and gets intense/shouty at higher volumes.

name: SeeAudio x Zeos Rinko
rawName: SeeAudio x Zeos Rinko ($99) not rec
notes: Sharp, bright, too aggresive, sounds like an unrefined early KZ v-shape, planar timbre, unnatural vocal timbre, also very pricy for what you get, not rec

name: TANGZU FUDU VERSE 2
notes: Wha duh hali. Very wonky and unnatural timbre. Vocals are thin, hollow, sharp, and shouty. No bass. Treble is masked by uppermids. Horrible scaling. Great design/build/accesories, but tangzu dropped the ball on the sound.

name: TINHIFI T2 Plus
notes: A T2 with more low-end, and less sharp. Probably the best T2 next to DLC.

name: TINHIFI T2 DLC
notes: A T2 with more low-end, and less sharp. Similar to T2 Plus but with more uppermids.

name: TRN ST5
notes: Lots of bass. Slams hard. Replaced by Rosefinch. But bleeds into the mids. Tech is just ok.

name: Moondrop Variations WITH EQ
notes: WITH EQ (boosting the mid-bass dip and taming the vocals). Very clear with lots of detail. Sub-bass has a nice rumble and texture. Amazing treble extension and stage air. Female vocals are vibrant and shines. Mid-bass cut is real, affecting some genres and male vocals. Note-weight can be light.

name: XENNS TOP
notes: 300 Mesh Filter allows it to scale at higher volumes and is smoother overall. Even though the nozzle is bigger than the filter, the hole in the nozzle is actually the right size for the filter, so just aim correctly and you're good to go!

name: Simgot EA1000
notes: Gold nozzle+500 mesh filter+deep wide tips= close to perfection. Ranking is only relevant in context with specific genres like ballads, slow-rock, acousitcs, and indie.

name: FATFREQ x EA QUANTUM 300 Mesh + Blue Filter
rawName: FATFREQ x EA QUANTUM ($759) 300 Mesh + Blue Filter
notes: Bright and full sound, very detailed, sparkly, airy, tons of treble extenstion... 300 mesh filter + blue filters help tames the energy and allows it to scale better.

name: Kiwi Ears Quintet
notes: Slight hit in sharpness and note definition, but overall smoother playback, and mostly fixing the metallic timbre. 300 Mesh Filter.

name: Tanchjim Hana 2021 Modded
notes: Amazing bass set when modded, but slightly worse resolution/separation than Olina. Much better note-weight, low-end rumble, and slam than modded Olina/Airship. Low-end is super immersive at high-volume.

name: Sennheiser IE200
notes: A +3db at 50hz 0.1 Q, +1 db at 2500hz 3Q, +1db 3000hz 1 Q fixes soft bass, and drastically impoves midrange and vocal clarity. Actually competitive now. One of the best treble extension and dynamics (around its price category) now without an anemic low-end and recessed mids to drag it down.

name: Apple AirPods Pro
rawName: Apple AirPods Pro (EQ) ($250) outdated dont buy
notes: Better soundstage and clarity due to tweak to high and low-end extension. Vocals are more engaging as well.

name: Sony WF-1000XM4
notes: Bass no longer bleeds and feels bloated, staging has more air, but still lacking in separation and resolution.

name: Simgot EWP100 Modded
notes: Clean and neutral. Nothing wrong with it. 300 mesh filter mod.

name: OG CCA CRA
notes: Tanya filters fixes uppermids and adds more low-end. Scales better and notes sound more weighted and fuller.

name: 7hz Salnotes Zero Modded
notes: Incredibly tuned IEM. Natural vocals and decent treble extension but not overdone like the Chu, Olina, or Dusk; vocals are more laid back instead of forward. Imaging is average and soundstage needs width/more 3D but not a complaint at $20. Mod: Add filter on top - the thicker the filter the more bass and less uppermids/treble.

name: Moondrop Chu Modded
rawName: Moondrop Chu Modded ($20) outdated dont buy
notes: Not as technicial as Starfield/Aria but more enjoyable tuning. Double filter mod and bass tips improves bass and smoothens out mid-high frequencies and treble for louder/longer listening. Mod: Add filter on top - the thicker the filter the more bass and less uppermids/treble.

name: Tanchjim Zero Modded
rawName: Tanchjim Zero Modded ($20) outdated dont buy
notes: Super clean, neutral, and smooth dynamics. Not low-end focused, but amazing vocal and mid-range clarity with good treble extension. Tech is average. 2x Hana Filter mod helps lower uppermids that otherwise gets intense at higher volumes.

name: TGXear SERRATUS
notes: One of the best timbre and coherency I've ever heard. Everything sounds like real life. Perfect note-weight. HUGE soundstage with excellent height, width and depth, even wider than EJ and DM. Thumping low-end makesyour ears rumble. Vocals are powerful, but could be more open, and can be a bit warm with some songs. Centre-stage imaging with decent separation. Could use more treble air extension, and better separation. Also needs a lot of powa (300ohms), and fit may be an issue. Otherwise HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

name: RikuBuds - Grand Rider 1
notes: Great low-end, punchy and textured. Full sounding signature in general. A set that you should crank UP. Soundstage is more depth than wide. Very good with hiphop/R&B/Pop. Vocals are a bit muffled. Treble roll off removes details. Imaging and separation is average. Doesn't fit my ears unfortunately. Very fun and thick overall, just wish it had more clarity with better separation and imaging. This would be amazing as a hybrid or tri-bird using the same DD. Recommended EQ: High-shelf 2000Hz +3db/High-shelf 10KHz +2db both with Q-factor 1
